chapters.title: Positive Levi directions and q-complete neighbourhoods

conventions.label: levi
conventions.text: For a real C-infinity function u on an open subset of C^N, H_u(x)(xi,xi)=sum u_{z_j bar-z_k}(x) xi_j conjugate(xi_k). It is strongly q-convex when it has at least max(0,N-q+1) strictly positive directions. On a complex space this means local ambient smooth extensions with that property.

conventions.label: exhaustion
conventions.text: A real continuous function bounded below whose sublevel sets {u<=c} are compact for every real c. A strongly q-complete space admits a smooth strongly q-convex exhaustion.

proofs.title: Coordinate compatibility and the shared-positive-subspace rule
proofs.statement: Strong q-convexity transfers between local embeddings. If H_u and H_w are positive on the same subspace F of dimension at least N-q+1, then u+theta(w) is strongly q-convex for every smooth convex nondecreasing theta.
proof: For a complex submanifold of dimension k in C^N, a positive subspace F of dimension N-q+1 intersects its tangent space in dimension at least k-q+1. Pullback by the holomorphic inclusion restricts the Levi form; this proves the restriction assertion, including the vacuous case k<q.

For two local embeddings G:U->A in C^N and G':U'->A' in C^M, lift the coordinate expressions of their inverse local isomorphisms to holomorphic maps P:W->C^M and Q:W'->W. They agree with G'G^{-1} and GG'^{-1} on the respective analytic sets. The smooth function U(z,w)=u(z)+|w-P(z)|^2 is the pullback of u(z)+|w|^2 by the biholomorphism (z,w)->(z,w-P(z)). It has at least N+M-q+1 positive directions. Restrict it along the holomorphic graph embedding w->(Q(w),w). The resulting extension u'(w)=u(Q(w))+|w-P(Q(w))|^2 has the required Levi index and equals the original function on A'. This also permits all functions in a comparison to be represented in a common ambient chart.

The chain rule gives H_{u+theta(w)}=H_u+theta'(w)H_w+theta''(w) partial-w tensor conjugate(partial-w). The last term is nonnegative and the middle term is nonnegative on F, while the first is positive there. Thus the same F works. The common subspace is essential: the two diagonal forms (-2,1,1) and (1,-2,1) on C^3 each have two positive directions, whereas their sum (-1,-1,2) has only one. We will not use a general closure of q-convex functions under addition.

proofs.title: Locally finite smooth constructions and closed strata
proofs.statement: The local models supply smooth cutoffs, a proper exhaustion and a finite closed filtration Z_{-1}=empty subset Z_0 subset ... subset Z_d=Y with Z_k minus Z_{k-1} a smooth k-dimensional manifold.
proof: The local models are locally compact and metrizable. A countable collection of precompact chart interiors gives compact sets K_j with K_j contained in the interior of K_{j+1} and union X: enlarge each finite union to include a precompact neighbourhood of the preceding compact set. Cover each compact annulus by finitely many still smaller chart balls, with supports confined to its neighbouring annuli. This constructs globally locally finite precompact refinements of any open cover, and the same construction works for a closed subset using its intersections with the annuli.

Restrict ordinary smooth Euclidean bumps to X. For a locally finite family of bumps whose positive sets cover X, divide their squares by their positive sum of squares. The resulting partition is smooth, nonnegative and locally finite; its functions have nonnegative local ambient extensions, by the same squared formula. A finite version supplies a cutoff equal to one on a compact set and supported inside any specified open neighbourhood. The annular refinement supplies the analogous cutoff for a closed set in an open set. A smooth function on a closed analytic set extends to X: take local smooth extensions, multiply by a partition subordinate to those charts and X minus Y, and sum. On Y every summand extends the same value.

Choose cutoffs chi_j equal to one near K_j and supported in the interior of K_{j+1}. The sum tau=sum_j(1-chi_j) is locally finite: all sufficiently large j have chi_j=1 near any fixed point. It is smooth and nonnegative. Outside K_{n+1}, its first n terms equal one, so {tau<=c} lies in a compact K_{n+1} when n>c. Its closed sublevels are therefore compact.

Start with Z_d=Y. Given an analytic Z_k of dimension at most k, let Z_{k-1} consist of its singular locus and all its irreducible components of dimension less than k. These sets are analytic and closed. Locally this uses finitely many component germs from Proposition 1.2; after shrinking their representatives, the selections agree on overlaps because local irreducible components and their dimensions agree there. A locally finite union of such components is analytic. The singular locus has smaller dimension on each component, by Theorem 3.3 and Proposition 5.5. Thus dim Z_{k-1}<=k-1, and the remaining regular components have dimension k. Iterate to Z_{-1}=empty; a reduced zero-dimensional analytic set is locally a point. Only this finite filtration is used below.

proofs.title: A small perturbation with an arbitrarily large normal Levi form
proofs.statement: For a holomorphic vector g and 0<epsilon<=1/2 put f_epsilon(g)=epsilon^3 log(1+|g|^2/epsilon^4). On a fixed compact chart f_epsilon and its first derivatives tend to zero, its Levi form is nonnegative, and at g=0 that form is epsilon^{-1} times the squared differential of g. A nonnegative cutoff changes the lower Levi bound by at most C epsilon.
proof: Write s=|g|^2. In the g coordinates the Levi matrix is epsilon^3[I/(epsilon^4+s) - conjugate(g) g^t/(epsilon^4+s)^2]. Its eigenvalues are epsilon^3/(epsilon^4+s) in directions perpendicular to g and epsilon^7/(epsilon^4+s)^2 in its radial direction. They are positive; holomorphic pullback therefore gives a nonnegative form. At g=0 the matrix is epsilon^{-1}I, giving the stated normal form even if g has a nontrivial kernel.

If |g|<=M and its differential is bounded on the chart, then 0<=f_epsilon<=epsilon^3 log(1+M^2/epsilon^4), which tends to zero. Its differential has norm at most a fixed constant times epsilon, because r/(epsilon^4+r^2)<=1/(2 epsilon^2); this inequality is precisely (r-epsilon^2)^2>=0. Also epsilon^3 log(1+M^2/epsilon^4)<=C_M epsilon for 0<epsilon<=1/2. These constants depend on the chosen compact chart, not on epsilon.

For a fixed nonnegative smooth theta, the product rule writes H_{theta f}=theta H_f+f H_theta+the two mixed first-derivative terms. The first term is nonnegative. The value and gradient bounds put the sum of the remaining terms above -C epsilon times the Euclidean Hermitian form. At g=0, both f and df vanish, so the exact identity is H_{theta f}=theta epsilon^{-1}(dg)^*dg. Thus a cutoff perturbation can be uniformly small in value and harmful Levi part while being arbitrarily positive in normal directions.

proofs.title: Stratified extension with simultaneous parameter choices
proofs.statement: If psi is smooth and strongly q-convex on Y and delta:Y->(0,infinity) is continuous, there is a neighbourhood W_0 of Y and a smooth strongly q-convex phi on W_0 satisfying psi<=phi|Y<psi+delta.
proof: Extend psi smoothly to X by QN-1, calling the extension phi_{-1}. It is strongly q-convex along Y in the sense that its restriction to Y has the required ambient extensions. Set V_{-1}=empty. Inductively maintain a global smooth phi_{k-1}, a closed neighbourhood V_{k-1} of Z_{k-1}, strong q-convexity on an open neighbourhood of V_{k-1}, strong q-convexity of phi_{k-1}|Y, and psi<=phi_{k-1}|Y<psi+delta.

Use the CLOSED set S=Z_k minus interior(V_{k-1}), not Z_k minus V_{k-1}. Since Z_{k-1} lies in the interior, S lies in the smooth k-dimensional stratum. Cover S by a globally locally finite family of precompact embedded charts A_lambda avoiding Z_{k-1}. In a larger ambient chart, Z_k is defined by normal coordinates g_lambda=(z_{k+1},...,z_N). Choose nonnegative smooth theta_lambda compactly supported in A_lambda, with sum theta_lambda=1 on S. A partition for the cover consisting of these charts and X minus S constructs these functions; the extra partition terms vanish on S. Choose the squared-bump construction so their local ambient extensions remain nonnegative.

Set phi_k=phi_{k-1}+sum_lambda theta_lambda f_{epsilon_lambda}(g_lambda), extending each compactly supported summand by zero. This is a locally finite smooth sum. On Y the increments are nonnegative. Its residual upper margin R=psi+delta-phi_{k-1}|Y is positive. On each compact test patch meeting Y the minimum of R on the relevant closed part of Y is positive, so an appropriately small sum of the value bounds in QN-2 keeps the new increment below R/2 there.

For preservation of the old positive directions, cover the closed set Y union V_{k-1} by locally finite precompact test patches. At a point of V_{k-1} choose a strongly q-convex ambient extension of phi_{k-1}; at other points of Y choose an extension of phi_{k-1}|Y. On a sufficiently small closed test patch its chosen positive subspace has a uniform positive lower bound a_j. All finitely many perturbations meeting that patch admit compatible holomorphic coordinate extensions and nonnegative cutoff extensions there, by QN-0 and QN-1. The harmful Levi part is bounded by sum_lambda C_{j,lambda} epsilon_lambda. Require this to be less than a_j/2. This preserves positivity on that same subspace. Outside the union of the supports nothing changes.

New positivity on S uses the exact zero-set identity of QN-2. Fix a small test patch on S with one theta_mu>=c_mu>0. All g_lambda vanish on Z_k there, so all added Levi terms at Z_k are nonnegative, and the mu term is at least t times the normal metric, t=c_mu/epsilon_mu. The tangential restriction of H_{phi_{k-1}} has a positive subspace F of dimension max(0,k-q+1), by QN-0. If F is nonzero, choose uniform bounds a>0 for its positive part, b for its mixed tangent-normal block, and -c for the normal block. For u in F and normal v, the perturbed form is at least a|u|^2-2b|u||v|+(t-c)|v|^2, which is at least (a/2)|u|^2+(t-c-2b^2/a)|v|^2. Taking t>c+2b^2/a makes it positive on F plus the whole normal space. If F is zero, t>c suffices on the normal space. The resulting dimension max(0,k-q+1)+N-k is at least max(0,N-q+1). Positivity is open, so this proves strong q-convexity on a neighbourhood of S.

Here is a simultaneous choice, not merely a pointwise instruction to take epsilon small. Use a globally locally finite precompact refinement of all the preceding preservation, margin and new-positivity test patches. Each such compact test patch meets only finitely many compact bump supports; each compact bump support meets only finitely many test patches. On a preservation patch with m_j incident bumps, allocate each at most a_j/(2m_j) of the harmful Levi bound, and similarly split the positive value margin. On a new-positivity patch impose the displayed upper bound on its chosen epsilon_mu. Consequently each individual epsilon_lambda is subject to only finitely many positive upper bounds. Choose it smaller than their minimum and 1/2. All conditions then hold at once, with no global uniform gap or zero parameter assumed.

The resulting function is strongly q-convex on some open O containing V_{k-1} union Z_k. That union is closed. Shrink around it, using normality of the metrizable space, to a closed neighbourhood V_k contained in O and containing the union in its interior. This restores the precise induction hypothesis; a union of a closed set with an arbitrary open neighbourhood is not asserted to be closed. There are d+1 stages. The final function is strongly q-convex on an open W_0 containing Y, and all the inequalities persist. No infinite limiting induction is invoked in this finite-dimensional application.

proofs.title: A logarithmic pole barrier with a locally bounded negative Levi part
proofs.statement: There is a function v on X, smooth off Y, with value minus infinity on Y, locally of the form log|g|^2+O(1) for generators of its ideal, and with a local ambient extension whose Levi form is bounded below off its pole set.
proof: Fix a smooth nonnegative probability density rho on (-1/2,1/2) with mean zero. For finitely many real numbers t_i define M(t)=integral max_i(t_i+s_i) product_i rho(s_i) ds. Convolution makes M smooth; convexity, monotonicity in every coordinate and translation equivariance follow from the same properties of max. Jensen's inequality and |s_i|<1/2 give max t_i<=M(t)<=max t_i+1/2. If one t_i is less than the maximum of the others by more than one, it cannot realize the maximum for any s in the support. Integration over its unused density equals one, so that coordinate drops exactly, not just approximately.

Choose a globally locally finite cover A_lambda=X intersect B(z_lambda,r_lambda) by precompact embedded balls, with larger charts around their closures. Coherence supplies finite holomorphic generator vectors g_lambda for the reduced ideal of Y on those larger charts. On A_lambda minus Y put v_lambda=log|g_lambda|^2-1/(r_lambda^2-|z-z_lambda|^2), and put v=M of the values whose patches contain the point. At a point of Y set v=-infinity.

Check the change of index set locally. If x is a boundary point of A_lambda, choose another patch A_mu containing x. On a sufficiently small compact neighbourhood of x inside the larger charts, each generator vector is a holomorphic matrix times the other, so their norms are bounded above and below by fixed multiples on X minus Y. This is a local compact-overlap assertion, not a uniform assertion on every entire overlap. The mu boundary penalty is bounded there, whereas the lambda penalty tends to minus infinity. Hence v_lambda<v_mu-1 sufficiently near that boundary. QN-4's exact coordinate-drop property removes lambda. Local finiteness leaves a fixed finite collection of active smooth expressions near every point off Y. Thus v is smooth there.

Near a point of Y the active generator norms are comparable with one fixed generator norm. The active smooth penalties are bounded and M differs from their maximum by at most 1/2. This proves v=log|g|^2+O(1) locally and v tends to minus infinity at Y. If Y contains a whole local component, this permits v identically minus infinity there; the final construction is identically phi on a neighbourhood of each such point.

Use holomorphic lifts of the active generators in one common ambient chart. Each logarithmic norm is plurisubharmonic: its Levi form is the nonnegative radial matrix obtained by differentiating log(|g|^2+eta) and letting eta decrease to zero. Add C|z|^2 to compensate the finitely many smooth penalties on a smaller relatively compact ambient chart. The chain rule for a smooth convex increasing M gives a sum of nonnegative Levi forms plus a nonnegative gradient quadratic form. Its translation property therefore shows H_v>=-C I off the poles. At poles take the decreasing limit using log(|g|^2+eta); the submean inequality passes to the limit (subtract a local upper bound and use monotone convergence). This supplies the local almost-plurisubharmonic extension, allowing the identically minus-infinity case. No integral estimate, vanishing theorem or q-complete neighbourhood result was used.

proofs.title: The neighbourhood exhaustion, with its properness proof
proofs.statement: If psi is a strongly q-convex exhaustion of Y, every open neighbourhood N of Y contains an open V on which there is a smooth strongly q-convex exhaustion h. It can be chosen with psi<=h|Y<psi+1.
proof: Apply QN-3 with delta=1, giving phi on W_0. Its restriction to Y is an exhaustion: {phi|Y<=c} is a closed subset of the compact set {psi<=c}. It is bounded below. Choose m below its infimum and use the proper tau of QN-1. There exists a positive increasing continuous function a on R with tau(y)<a(phi(y)) for every y in Y: the suprema of tau on compact sublevels of phi|Y are finite, and an increasing polygonal majorant with a one-level look-ahead bounds them strictly. Thus O={x in W_0: phi(x)>m and tau(x)<a(phi(x))} is an open neighbourhood of Y.

Choose an open W_1 containing Y whose closure in X is contained in O. On its closure phi is bounded below by m and proper: {x in closure(W_1):phi(x)<=c} is closed in X and lies in the compact set {tau<=a(c)}. This proves the thickening assertion rather than assuming it from properness only on Y. Now choose an open W with Y subset W and closure(W) subset W_1 intersect N. Its boundary is disjoint from Y.

Take the pole barrier v from QN-4. On each compact phi-sublevel in closure(W_1), finitely many common ambient charts give positive subspaces F_i for H_phi, positive gaps a_i, and lower bounds H_v>=-b_i I. The subspaces are fixed on sufficiently small individual charts, not globally identified between charts. For an increasing convex smooth function chi, H_{v+chi(phi)}=H_v+chi'(phi)H_phi+chi''(phi) partial-phi tensor conjugate(partial-phi). On F_i this is at least (-b_i+chi' a_i) times the metric. Choose chi' greater than all corresponding b_i/a_i. In charts with N_i<q the positivity condition is vacuous.

The choice can also impose v+chi(phi)>1 on boundary(W). On each compact sublevel the boundary is compact and disjoint from Y, so v has a finite minimum there. Both the derivative requirements and these value requirements are bounded on each interval [m,m+j]. To construct chi, take a nondecreasing sequence D_j>=1 dominating the derivative bounds and the positive parts of all required values on [m,m+j+3]. A nondecreasing smooth function exceeding D_j on [m+j,m+j+1] is obtained by summing nonnegative jumps times smooth increasing switches, each completed before m+j. Integrate this function to obtain chi. Choose chi(m) sufficiently large for the first compact interval. On every later interval the preceding unit interval contributes at least D_{j-1}, which dominates that interval's value requirement. Thus chi, chi' and chi'' have all the required properties, including chi''>=0.

Write nu=v+chi(phi). It tends to minus infinity at Y, is greater than one on boundary(W), and its Levi form is positive on the SAME F_i as H_phi. Choose a nonnegative smooth eta on (-infinity,0) which is zero on (-infinity,-2] and equals 2/(-s)^3 on [-1,0). Define theta(t)=integral from minus infinity to t of (t-s)eta(s) ds. Then theta is smooth, convex, nondecreasing, zero for t<=-2 and diverges to positive infinity as t increases to zero; on [-1,0) it is -1/t plus an affine function. Put V={x in W:nu(x)<0} and h=phi+theta(nu) there. Since nu tends to minus infinity locally at Y, h=phi near each point of Y and extends smoothly across Y. Away from Y QN-0 proves strong q-convexity using the same F_i; at Y it follows from phi. In particular psi<=h|Y<psi+1.

For properness, h>=phi>m. A sequence in {h<=c} has a subsequence converging in the compact set closure(W_1) intersect {phi<=c}. Its limit lies in closure(W). It cannot lie on boundary(W), since nu>1 there and nu is continuous off Y. If its limit lies in W minus Y, then nu<=0; equality is impossible because theta(nu) would diverge while phi remains bounded below. A limit in Y already belongs to V and h is smooth near it. Thus every limit lies in V, and continuity makes {h<=c} closed there. It is consequently compact. This proves that h is an exhaustion and that V is strongly q-complete. Since N was arbitrary the neighbourhoods form a fundamental family. If Y is empty, take V empty; this separate trivial case avoids taking an infimum over an empty set.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: For each form degree k, D_k is maximal distributional dbar: L2_(n,k)(M,E,h exp(-Phi),omega_tilde) -> L2_(n,k+1), with domain those forms whose distributional derivative is in the target L2 space. D_n=0 on the entire top-degree space. The formal weighted adjoint from degree k to k-1 is delta_k; WL-1 proves delta_k=D_(k-1)^* on the relevant maximal domain.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: The compactly supported Hilbert inner product is linear in its first variable. Adjoint identities use that convention. Let L be exterior multiplication by omega_tilde and Lambda=L*. For operators of total-degree parity a,b, [A,B]=AB-(-1)^(ab)BA. A differential form inside a commutator denotes its exterior-multiplication operator.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: The Chern curvature convention is D_E^2=Theta(E); in a holomorphic frame with metric matrix h, its (1,0) connection matrix is h^(-1) partial h. For h_Phi=exp(-Phi)h, Theta(E_Phi)=Theta(E)+partial dbar Phi times Id. The real (1,1) curvature form is iTheta.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: For the fixed base metric omega_tilde, T=[Lambda,[Lambda,(i/2)partial dbar omega_tilde]]-[partial omega_tilde,(partial omega_tilde)*]. This is a smooth zero-order self-adjoint endomorphism in the source identity. It acts trivially on the E factor and therefore does not change when the bundle metric is multiplied by exp(-Phi). Its occurrence is not suppressed by pretending omega_tilde is Kahler.

proofs.title: An adapted metric with quantitative sums of Levi eigenvalues
proofs.statement: For 1<=q<=n and epsilon=1/(2q), there is a smooth Hermitian metric omega for which every Levi eigenvalue of psi is >=-epsilon and the largest n-q+1 equal 1. Consequently every sum of k>=q eigenvalues is >=c_q=1-(q-1)/(2q)>1/2.
proof: Start with any smooth Hermitian metric omega_0, constructed by locally finite positive partitions of chart metrics. Write its Levi endomorphism as A_0 and its ordered eigenvalues as gamma_1<=...<=gamma_n. The finite Hermitian spectral theorem follows by maximizing the real Rayleigh quotient on the complex unit sphere: variations in w and iw show that a maximizer is an eigenvector, its orthogonal complement is invariant, and induction diagonalizes A_0. The eigenvalue min-max characterization follows by intersecting a test subspace with the spans of the first or last eigenvectors. It gives |gamma_j(A)-gamma_j(B)|<=||A-B||, so gamma_q is continuous and strictly positive. Refine into precompact sets on each of which gamma_q exceeds a positive constant 2b_alpha, take a subordinate partition lambda_alpha, and put eta=sum lambda_alpha b_alpha. Then eta is smooth and 0<eta<=gamma_q/2.

Choose a smooth function beta equal to 1 for t<=0, equal to 0 for t>=1, and between 0 and 1. Put a=1+epsilon^(-1) and theta(t)=t+beta(t) exp(-at). It is positive: for t<0, exp(a|t|)>=a|t|, hence theta(t)>=|t|/epsilon; at t=0 it is 1; and for t>0 it is at least t. Also theta(t)=t for t>=1. Define the positive endomorphism A=eta theta(eta^(-1) A_0), and set omega(v,w)=omega_0(Av,w).

This construction is smooth even at repeated eigenvalues. In a smooth omega_0-orthonormal frame over a precompact chart, the spectra of eta^(-1)A_0 stay in one compact interval. Replace theta outside that interval by a compactly supported smooth scalar function f. The exact spectral formula f(B)=(2pi)^(-1) integral Ff(t) exp(itB)dt follows by diagonalizing the fixed matrix B and applying the one-dimensional inversion theorem. Differentiating exp(itB(x)) once gives i integral_0^t exp(i(t-s)B)(partial B)exp(isB)ds; repeated parameter derivatives have polynomial growth in |t| on the chart because the exponentials are unitary. Ff decreases faster than each inverse polynomial, so differentiation under the integral is justified to every order. The formula is equivariant under frame changes, proving smoothness of A independently of eigenvector choices.

The new eigenvalues are lambda_j=gamma_j/[eta theta(gamma_j/eta)]. If gamma_j<0, the bound on theta gives lambda_j>=-epsilon. If gamma_j>=0, lambda_j>=0. For j>=q, gamma_j/eta>=1, so lambda_j=1. A set of k indices contains at least k-q+1 of these last indices; its sum is therefore at least k-q+1-(q-1)epsilon>=c_q. This proves the stated bound without adding two unrelated q-positive forms.

proofs.title: A complete metric and the actual joint graph domain
proofs.statement: The adapted metric admits a complete conformal enlargement. For every fixed smooth bundle weight, compactly supported smooth forms are dense for the joint graph norm of D and its weighted formal adjoint, which equals the Hilbert adjoint on its maximal distributional domain.
proof: Shift psi so psi>=0. With the real Riemannian norm induced by omega, set rho=log(1+|dpsi|_omega^2) and omega_tilde=exp(rho)omega. Then |dpsi|_omega_tilde<=1. Along any piecewise smooth path, the change of psi is no greater than its length. Thus a metric Cauchy sequence in a connected component has bounded psi and lies in a compact closed sublevel. It has a convergent subsequence in the manifold topology, which agrees locally with the metric topology; its Cauchy property gives convergence of the whole sequence. This proves completeness. Disconnected components cause no difficulty, since all arguments are componentwise and the exhaustion still has compact sublevels.

Take a smooth kappa equal to 1 on (-infinity,1], zero on [2,infinity), between 0 and 1, with bounded derivative, and set eta_j=kappa(psi/j), j>=1. Its support is compact, it tends locally to 1, and |deta_j|_omega_tilde<=||kappa'||_infinity/j. Distributional Leibniz rules give D(eta_j u)=eta_j Du+(dbar eta_j) wedge u and delta(eta_j u)=eta_j delta u-(exterior multiplication by dbar eta_j)*u. The adjoint in the last term is pointwise; it is unaffected by a common scalar bundle weight in adjacent degrees. Exterior multiplication and contraction have operator norm at most the covector norm. Hence the extra terms tend to zero in L2, and dominated convergence handles the three terms multiplied by eta_j. This proves graph approximation by compactly supported forms, with no uniform bound on derivatives of Phi required.

For such a compact support, choose finitely many relatively compact charts, smooth bundle frames and a subordinate partition. Each localized component has D and delta in L2 because partition commutators are zero-order. In a chart these are finite matrices of first-order operators with smooth coefficients. Apply the complete commutator proof of the imported Friedrichs Lemma 3.1 entry by entry to ordinary convolution. Both operators then converge in L2 together with the form; the finitely many chart metrics and weights are bounded above and below, so the same holds in their weighted norms. Sum the smooth approximants and choose a diagonal sequence after the eta_j cutoff. This proves density in the joint maximal graph domain, and separately in the maximal D graph domain.

If u is in the Hilbert-adjoint domain of D, testing against compactly supported smooth forms identifies D*u with the formal adjoint delta u as a distribution. Conversely, if u and delta u are in L2, integrate by parts against compactly supported smooth v and pass to every v in the maximal D domain using the just-proved graph density. The identity (Dv,u)=(v,delta u) gives u in Dom D* with D*u=delta u. Maximal distributional D is closed: convergence of u_j and Du_j in L2 implies convergence on compactly supported distribution tests. Its kernel is closed, its domain is dense, and D_(k+1)D_k=0 whenever the first derivative lies in L2, because dbar squared is zero in each holomorphic frame. These are the exact Hilbert-complex hypotheses used in WL-4.

proofs.title: Local first-order ellipticity from L2, with fixed-coefficient interior bounds
proofs.statement: For Q=(D,delta) at any fixed degree and with fixed smooth metrics and weight, u in L2_loc and Qu smooth imply u smooth. If Qu=0 on an open V containing a compact K, every C^ell(K) norm of u is bounded by C_(ell,K,V)||u||_L2(V') for a relatively compact intermediate neighbourhood V' of K in V. The constants depend on the fixed local coefficients, not on u.
proof: For a real cotangent vector xi, the two principal symbols are exterior multiplication by zeta=xi^(0,1), up to a unit scalar, and its adjoint contraction. Their squared norms on a vector v add to |zeta|^2|v|^2. To verify this, if zeta is nonzero extend zeta/|zeta| to a unitary coframe and write v as the sum of its first-covector factor and its part with no such factor; these two parts are orthogonal, and the two operations extract their complementary norms. For real xi, zeta is nonzero whenever xi is nonzero, with |zeta|^2 a fixed positive multiple of |xi|^2 in the induced convention. Bundle and (n,0) factors are spectators. Thus Q has an injective real principal symbol in every degree, including degree zero and top degree.

Write Q=sum A_j(x)partial_j+B(x) in smooth coordinate frames and freeze its principal coefficients at a point x_0. Plancherel from the imported Fourier theorem, applied to compactly supported smooth vector functions, gives ||grad v||_2<=C||sum A_j(x_0)partial_j v||_2. Indeed the pointwise symbol lower bound controls |xi|^2|Fv(xi)|^2, and the common (2pi)^d factor cancels upon integration. Shrink the ball so C sum_j sup||A_j(x)-A_j(x_0)||<1/2. The difference from Q is the small principal part plus bounded Bv. Move the former term to the left to obtain ||v||_H1<=C_1(||Qv||_2+||v||_2) for compactly supported smooth v in this ball. Smooth densities and fibre norms are uniformly comparable on its closure; they change C_1 but not the estimate.

Now suppose only u and Qu are L2 locally. Multiply by a compact cutoff in the ball; Q(chi u)=chi Qu+[Q,chi]u is L2. By the matrix Friedrichs argument in WL-1, its smooth convolutions v_j converge with Qv_j in L2 and have support in a fixed smaller ball. Apply the preceding estimate to v_j-v_l. They are Cauchy in H1, and their L2 limit is chi u; closedness of distributional derivatives identifies the H1 limit. Thus u is H1 on the region where chi=1. This supplies the missing initial derivative, rather than assuming it.

If u is H^m locally and Qu is H^m locally, differentiate a multi-index alpha of length m: Q partial^alpha u=partial^alpha(Qu)-[partial^alpha,Q]u as distributions. Expanding the commutator by the finite Leibniz rule gives only derivatives of u of order at most m: whenever a derivative hits a principal coefficient, the order on u drops by at least one before the one derivative already in Q is counted. All coefficients and their finitely many derivatives are bounded on a smaller compact chart. The base H1 argument applied to each partial^alpha u proves u in H^(m+1) locally. Induction gives all Sobolev orders when Qu is smooth. The same estimates, with nested cutoffs and a finite chart cover, give ||u||_Hm(K_neighbourhood)<=C_m||u||_L2(V') in the homogeneous case; at step m each cutoff or coefficient commutator is bounded by the preceding Hm norm on a slightly larger neighbourhood. One chooses finitely many nested neighbourhoods for each specified m, not a single constant for all m.

For compactly supported smooth v on R^d and s>ell+d/2, the imported Fourier weight formula and Cauchy-Schwarz give integral |xi|^ell|Fv(xi)|dx<=C||v||_Hs: the square of |xi|^ell(1+|xi|^2)^(-s/2) is integrable by the same annular estimate as in Section 2. Fourier inversion therefore bounds all derivatives through order ell uniformly. Extend to Hs by smooth convolution and cutoff approximation; the uniform derivative limits agree with distributional derivatives. Apply this to local cutoffs of u and the preceding Hs estimate. This proves smoothness and the asserted C^ell interior bound. The proof is local on a possibly noncompact manifold and does not import a compact-manifold Garding statement with incompatible hypotheses.

proofs.title: Levi action on top holomorphic degree and actual weight selection
proofs.statement: For every holomorphic Hermitian E on M with 1<=q<=n, one can choose a smooth convex increasing chi_0 such that A_(chi_0,k)=[iTheta(E_(chi_0 composed with psi)),Lambda]+T>=Id on (n,k)-forms for every k>=q. Adding any convex nondecreasing function of psi preserves this. Given smooth g, an additional such weight can make g square integrable.
proof: At one point choose a unitary coframe zeta_j diagonalizing a real (1,1) form beta=i sum lambda_j zeta_j wedge bar(zeta_j). The identities for exterior multiplication e_j and its adjoint i_j are e_j i_j+i_j e_j=Id and anticommutation between different indices. Thus [beta wedge,Lambda] on zeta_I wedge bar(zeta_J) has eigenvalue sum_(j in I)lambda_j+sum_(j in J)lambda_j-sum_all lambda_j: in each index the pair commutator is +1 if both covectors occur, -1 if neither occurs, and zero if exactly one occurs; different pair indices commute. For holomorphic degree n, this becomes sum_(j in J)lambda_j. Under omega_tilde=exp(rho)omega, every Levi eigenvalue scales by exp(-rho), so WL-0 gives the lower bound c_q exp(-rho) on every (n,k), k>=q. A positive semidefinite (1,1) form likewise has nonnegative action in these degrees; that assertion is not being extended to arbitrary (p,k).

In a holomorphic frame, h_Phi^(-1)partial h_Phi=h^(-1)partial h-partial Phi Id. Differentiating with dbar gives Theta(E_Phi)=Theta(E)+partial dbar Phi Id, since dbar partial Phi=-partial dbar Phi. The chain rule for Phi=chi(psi) gives i partial dbar Phi=chi'(psi)i partial dbar psi+chi''(psi)i partial psi wedge dbar psi. The latter summand is positive semidefinite if chi''>=0. The zero-order endomorphisms B_k=[iTheta(E),Lambda]+T have locally bounded norms for the fixed metric. Choose a positive smooth function a larger than all these finitely many norms by a locally finite partition with upper bounds on precompact supports. Then A_(chi,k)>=(-a+c_q exp(-rho)chi'(psi))Id for k>=q. This is only an algebraic inequality between zero-order operators; the analytic basic inequality is the separate input in WL-4.

Here is an explicit smooth convex majorant construction. For every integer j>=0 let a_j>=1 be a nondecreasing sequence exceeding the supremum of (a+1)exp(rho)/c_q on {psi<=j+2}. Let sigma be smooth nondecreasing, zero for t<=0 and one for t>=1. Set h(t)=a_0+sum_(j>=1)(a_j-a_(j-1))sigma(t-j+1), a locally finite smooth sum, and chi_0(t)=integral_0^t h(s)ds. For t in [j,j+1], h(t)>=a_j; also h'>=0. Thus chi_0 is increasing and convex and the desired operator lower bound is >=1. Adding chi_1 with nonnegative first and second derivatives contributes a nonnegative operator by the sum-of-eigenvalues bound just proved, even though the Levi form itself need not be positive semidefinite.

For a smooth g in any of the relevant degrees, set M_j=integral_(psi<=j+1)|g|^2 exp(-chi_0(psi))dV, finite by compactness. Choose nonnegative b_j>=j+log(1+M_j). Apply the preceding smooth nondecreasing construction to produce h_1 with h_1(t)>=b_(j+1) on [j,j+1], taking nondecreasing maxima of the b values first. Put chi_1(t)=b_0+integral_0^t h_1(s)ds. It is convex nondecreasing, and chi_1(j)>=b_j for every integer j (for j>=1 use its last unit interval). On the shell j<=psi<j+1, the new integral is at most exp(-b_j)M_j<=exp(-j). Summing proves g in L2 for Phi=(chi_0+chi_1)(psi), while preserving A>=Id. The weight depends on g; no unjustified universal integrability claim is made.

proofs.title: Weighted solvability and smooth minimal solutions, conditional only at the indicated curvature step
proofs.statement: Assume the compact-support Hermitian curvature inequality BKN-HERMITIAN-TORSION below. For any weight in WL-3, every closed g in L2_(n,k), k>=q, has a distributional solution f in L2_(n,k-1) with Df=g and ||f||<=||g||. The minimal-norm solution satisfies delta f=0 and is smooth when g is smooth.
proof: The explicitly retained input is ||Du||^2+||delta u||^2>=integral <A_(Phi,k)u,u>dV for every smooth compactly supported u. For clarity, the right side includes the bundle weight through the fibre metric. It follows from the full non-Kahler identity with T, not the Euclidean scalar identity. Given this input, A>=Id implies ||Du||^2+||delta u||^2>=||u||^2 on compact forms. WL-1 passes this inequality to Dom D_k intersect Dom D_(k-1)^* by joint graph convergence. No unbounded-curvature integral limit is needed after the pointwise lower bound has been applied.

Use the existing Hilbert Lemma 1.1 with H_1 degree k-1, H_2 degree k, H_3 degree k+1, T=D_(k-1), S=D_k and C=1. Its orthogonal decomposition uses the closed space ker S, not a presumed closed range of T. WL-1 verifies every domain and adjoint hypothesis. The lemma supplies f with (f,T*u)=(g,u); testing compact forms identifies Tf=g distributionally, and since g belongs to H_2 this places f in the maximal domain. The bound is ||f||<=||g||.

The solution set is a nonempty closed affine translate of ker T in H_1. Orthogonal projection gives its unique minimum-norm element f_min, which is perpendicular to ker T. The image of R=D_(k-2) lies in ker T, so (Rv,f_min)=0 for every v in Dom R. By the definition of the Hilbert adjoint, f_min is in Dom R* and R*f_min=0; if k=1 there is no preceding degree and this equation is vacuous. Thus Qf_min=(g,0), with Q=(D,delta) at degree k-1. It is initially L2_loc, and all the metric and weight coefficients are smooth. WL-2 proves it smooth whenever g is smooth, without assuming the initial H1 regularity or first asserting an unproved second-order elliptic estimate.

proofs.title: The full bundle twist and the degree endpoints for manifold vanishing
proofs.statement: Assuming the same curvature input, H^k(M,O(E))=0 for k>=q on a strongly q-complete complex n-manifold, without assuming K_M trivial or the metric Kahler.
proof: For 1<=q<=n, replace E in WL-0 through WL-4 by F=K_M^(-1) tensor E. There is a canonical holomorphic-bundle identification Lambda^(n,k)T*M tensor F = Lambda^(0,k)T*M tensor E: contract K_M with its dual. In local holomorphic frames the contraction commutes with dbar, so it is an isomorphism of the entire smooth Dolbeault complexes, not just of their fibres. Equip F with any smooth Hermitian metric. For each smooth closed E-valued (0,k) form, k>=q, use this identification, choose its integrability weight by WL-3, and obtain a smooth primitive by WL-4. Transport back. The existing Dolbeault Theorem 3.2 identifies the resulting vanishing quotient with H^k(M,O(E)).

When k>n, the smooth resolution has no term of that degree and the same programme theorem gives zero directly. Hence q>n is fully included without inventing a positive gamma_q eigenvalue. The case n=0 is also covered by this last observation for every q>=1. These statements concern arbitrary finite-rank holomorphic bundles. They do not by themselves prove coherent-sheaf vanishing on singular spaces or derived base change; those remain separate steps.

proofs.title: Degree-(q-1) approximation with uniform inner estimates
proofs.statement: Suppose U is an open subset of M such that for every compact L in U there is a strongly q-complete exhaustion psi of M and numbers b_0<b with L subset M_(b_0), closure M_(b_0) subset M_b, and closure M_b compact in U, where M_c={psi<c}. Then every smooth closed E-valued (0,q-1)-form h on U is the C-infinity-local limit of restrictions of globally closed smooth forms on M.
proof: First take 1<=q<=n and one such compact L. Perform the K_M^(-1) twist from WL-5. Choose eta smooth compactly supported in U, equal to 1 on a neighbourhood of closure M_b. Extend eta h by zero to M and put g=D(eta h). Since Dh=0 on U, g is smooth, compactly supported, D-closed, and vanishes on a neighbourhood of closure M_b. Choose the metric and chi_0 from WL-0 through WL-3 for this exhaustion and bundle. The weight chi_0 alone suffices for the compactly supported g.

Let a smooth nonnegative function alpha vanish on (-infinity,b_0] and be strictly positive on (b_0,infinity), for example alpha(t)=exp(-1/(t-b_0)^2) there. Define theta(t) as zero for t<=b_0 and c integral_(b_0)^t (t-s)alpha(s)ds otherwise, with c>0 chosen so theta(b)=1. It is smooth, convex, nondecreasing, identically zero on t<=b_0 and >=1 on t>=b. The correctly typed scalar weights are chi_nu(t)=chi_0(t)+nu theta(t) and Phi_nu(x)=chi_nu(psi(x)); neither rho composed with psi nor a mixture of scalar and manifold variables is used.

WL-3 keeps A>=Id for all nu. Let f_nu be the smooth minimum-norm solution of Df_nu=g supplied by WL-4 with weight Phi_nu. Since support g is in {psi>=b}, its squared norm is <=C exp(-nu), where C=integral |g|^2 exp(-chi_0(psi))dV is independent of nu. The same bound holds for f_nu in its global weighted norm. On M_(b_0), Phi_nu=Phi_0 as smooth functions, including all derivatives; thus the weighted adjoints there are exactly the fixed delta_0, not just bounded relatives. Consequently Df_nu=0 and delta_0 f_nu=0 there, and ||f_nu||^2_(L2(M_(b_0),Phi_0))<=C exp(-nu).

Choose fixed compact neighbourhoods L subset V' with closure V' in M_(b_0). Smooth metric and weight equivalence on V', followed by WL-2 for the fixed system (D,delta_0), gives ||f_nu||_(C^ell(L))<=C_ell exp(-nu/2) for every ell. No coefficient in this interior estimate varies with nu. The forms h_nu=eta h-f_nu are globally D-closed; on L, eta=1, so h_nu-h=-f_nu. This proves approximation on L to any finite list of derivatives.

Choose a compact exhaustion L_j of U with interiors covering U and increasing. For each j perform the preceding construction anew, and choose nu_j so the difference is <2^(-j) in all the first j prescribed chart C^ell seminorms on L_j. A fixed enumeration of relatively compact chart seminorms defines the C-infinity-local topology. Its first r seminorms are controlled once j>=r; therefore this diagonal sequence converges to h in that topology. The metrics and exhaustions can vary with j, because the constants are required to be uniform only in nu within each individual construction.

If q=n+1, h has top antiholomorphic degree n, so D of any such smooth form is zero for degree reasons. Compactly supported cutoffs eta_j equal to 1 on L_j give globally smooth, globally closed extensions eta_j h and exact agreement on each eventual compact set. If q>n+1 the form space itself is zero. These cases include n=0 and prove the endpoints without misusing the eigenvalue or solvability argument.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: D=D'+D'' is the Chern connection, extended to E-valued exterior forms by the graded Leibniz rule. Set C=D', B=D'', a=(D')*, b=(D'')*, where star means formal L2 adjoint. The inner product is linear in its first argument. Put L=omega wedge and Lambda=L* pointwise.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: P=(partial omega) wedge has bidegree (2,1) and total degree 3; Q=(dbar omega) wedge has bidegree (1,2). Define tau=[Lambda,P] and sigma=[Lambda,Q]. On scalar forms sigma is the conjugate of tau. On bundle-valued forms both act as these same scalar endomorphisms tensor Id_E. In particular sigma* and tau* are distinct operators and may not be interchanged.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: The bracket is graded by total degree parity: [U,V]=UV-(-1)^(deg U deg V)VU. Thus all brackets between C,B,a,b,tau,sigma or their adjoints are anticommutators, while brackets involving L or Lambda are ordinary commutators. A form appearing inside a bracket denotes exterior multiplication by that form.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Theta=D^2=[C,B] is curvature exterior multiplication. Delta''=[B,b], Delta'=[C,a], and Delta'_tau=[C+tau,a+tau*]. Define T=[Lambda,[Lambda,(i/2)partial dbar omega wedge]]-[P,P*].

proofs.title: Exterior algebra and graded identities with their signs
proofs.statement: On total degree r forms, H=[L,Lambda]=(r-n)Id. The graded Jacobi identity and adjoint reversal hold with the conventions above. For a constant unitary metric, [dbar*_0,L_0]=i partial and [Lambda_0,dbar*_0]=0.
proof: In a unitary coframe write e_j=dz_j wedge and f_j=dbar z_j wedge, with adjoints e_j* and f_j*. Exterior anticommutation gives e_j e_k+e_k e_j=0, e_j* e_k+e_k e_j*=delta_jk Id, and the analogous formulas for all holomorphic and antiholomorphic covectors. Here L=i sum e_j f_j and Lambda=-i sum f_j* e_j*. For each index, the pair commutator has value 1 when both covectors occur, -1 when neither occurs, and 0 when exactly one occurs. Distinct even pairs commute. Adding over j gives H=(r-n)Id. Therefore [H,U]=sU for an operator increasing total degree by s; the identity holds for differential operators as well since H is constant on each degree.

For homogeneous U,V,W of parities u,v,w, expand both sides of [U,[V,W]]=[[U,V],W]+(-1)^(uv)[V,[U,W]]. In the right side, the VUW terms cancel, as do the WUV terms. The terms left are UVW-(-1)^(vw)UWV-(-1)^(u(v+w))VWU+(-1)^(u(v+w)+vw)WVU, exactly the left side. This proves Jacobi without an external locator. Formal integration by parts and complex conjugation give (UV)*=V*U*, (iU)*=-iU*, and [U,V]*=[V*,U*].

For constant omega_0=i sum dz_j wedge dbar z_j, integration by parts in real coordinates gives dbar*_0=-sum f_j* partial_(z_j), while partial=sum e_j partial_(z_j). Anticommutation gives [f_j*,L_0]=-i e_j. Since L_0 has constant coefficients, [dbar*_0,L_0]=i partial. The contraction f_j* commutes with every even contraction pair f_k*e_k*, so [Lambda_0,dbar*_0]=0. These computations are identities on arbitrary smooth forms; only the derivation of the formal adjoint uses compact test functions.

proofs.title: The scalar Hermitian commutation formula without a Kahler normalization
proofs.statement: On scalar forms, [dbar*,L]=i(partial+tau), [partial*,L]=-i(dbar+sigma), [Lambda,dbar]=-i(partial*+tau*) and [Lambda,partial]=i(dbar*+sigma*).
proof: Fix a point x_0. A complex-linear coordinate change makes omega(x_0)=omega_0=i sum dz_j wedge dbar z_j, but does not remove the first derivatives of omega. Write gamma=omega-omega_0, so gamma(x_0)=0. Let M_(p,q)(x) be the matrix comparing the actual pointwise inner product times volume with the constant one on (p,q)-forms. Then M=Id-[gamma wedge,Lambda_0]+O(|x-x_0|^2). To compute its first derivative, diagonalize gamma at one point with eigenvalues gamma_j relative to omega_0. The coefficient of a basis form dz_I wedge dbar z_J in this density is product_all(1+gamma_j) divided by product_I(1+gamma_j) product_J(1+gamma_j). Its linear term is sum_all gamma_j-sum_I gamma_j-sum_J gamma_j, the negative of the commutator eigenvalue established in WL-3. This calculation determines the first derivative in every Hermitian direction. The actual matrix M is a smooth function of the entries of omega and their inverses, so its Taylor remainder is genuinely quadratic in smooth coordinates. No smooth choice of diagonalizing eigenvectors is assumed.

Put delta_0=dbar*_0. The actual formal adjoint is M_(p,q-1)^(-1) delta_0 M_(p,q), by integration by parts with the two density matrices. At x_0 this becomes delta=delta_0-[delta_0,[gamma,Lambda_0]], since gamma(x_0)=0 and the quadratic Taylor remainder has zero first derivative there. By Jacobi and [delta_0,Lambda_0]=0, this is delta_0+[Lambda_0,C_0], where C_0=[delta_0,gamma]. The correction is allowed to be a first-order operator away from x_0; its principal coefficients vanish at x_0. This distinction matters when forming the next commutator.

At x_0, expanding L=L_0+gamma gives [L,delta]=[L_0,delta_0]+[L_0,[Lambda_0,C_0]]+[gamma,delta_0]. The omitted correction with two factors gamma vanishes at x_0: its first-order part contains two zero factors, and differentiating at most one factor still leaves the other zero. Since [gamma,L_0]=0, Jacobi gives [C_0,L_0]=-[gamma,[delta_0,L_0]]=i(partial gamma) wedge. Thus [L_0,C_0]=-i(partial gamma) wedge. Also C_0 raises total degree by one, so [H_0,C_0]=C_0. Consequently [L_0,[Lambda_0,C_0]]=C_0-i[Lambda_0,partial gamma wedge]. The term C_0 cancels [gamma,delta_0]=-C_0. BK-0 now yields [L,delta]=-i partial-i[Lambda_0,partial gamma wedge]=-i(partial+tau) at x_0. Since x_0 was arbitrary, the first asserted identity holds everywhere.

Complex conjugation commutes with L and with the real Riemannian metric on scalar forms, interchanges partial and dbar, and sends i to -i and tau to sigma. It yields the second identity. Taking formal adjoints of the first and second identities, using BK-0, gives the third and fourth respectively. This establishes all four formulas with their conjugate-torsion terms. No coordinate system with vanishing metric derivatives, and hence no hidden Kahler assumption, has been used.

proofs.title: Chern connection and an explicit normal holomorphic bundle frame
proofs.statement: The scalar identities extend to E-valued forms as [b,L]=i(C+tau), [a,L]=-i(B+sigma), [Lambda,B]=-i(a+tau*) and [Lambda,C]=i(b+sigma*). Moreover C^2=B^2=0 and [C,B]=Theta.
proof: In a holomorphic frame let h be the positive Hermitian matrix and set A=h^(-1)partial h. Define C=partial+A wedge and B=dbar. Under a holomorphic frame change G, h becomes G^dagger h G and A becomes G^(-1)AG+G^(-1)partial G; dagger here means coefficientwise conjugate transpose, conjugating the differential for a matrix-valued form, not the formal operator adjoint. In particular partial G^dagger=0. These local formulas therefore define a connection on the bundle. Its metric compatibility follows from hA=partial h and A^dagger h=dbar h. The same identities show uniqueness among metric connections whose (0,1) part is the given holomorphic structure. Differentiating h^(-1) gives partial A=-A wedge A. Hence C^2=0, while B^2=0 in holomorphic frames. Their graded mixed commutator is dbar A wedge, which is the (1,1) Chern curvature Theta.

At a chosen point x_0, first use a constant frame change so h(x_0)=Id; positive square roots exist by finite Hermitian diagonalization. In holomorphic coordinates z centered at x_0, write H_j=partial h/partial z_j evaluated at x_0 and take G(z)=Id-sum H_j z_j. It is holomorphic and invertible after shrinking. The transformed metric h_1=G* h G satisfies h_1(x_0)=Id and partial h_1/partial z_j(x_0)=H_j-H_j=0. Hermitian symmetry also makes all antiholomorphic first derivatives zero. Therefore h_1=Id+O(|z|^2) and its connection matrix is O(|z|). This proves the needed frame statement rather than referring to the source's placeholder locator.

In this frame C and B at x_0 agree with scalar partial and dbar on each coefficient. The bundle contribution to the formal adjoints is obtained from the same density-matrix integration by parts as in BK-1; h_1-Id is quadratic and its first derivatives vanish, so the adjoints at x_0 also agree coefficientwise with the scalar ones. In a commutator with the zero-order L or Lambda, differences in these bundle operators vanish at x_0: their connection terms are zero-order O(|z|), and any principal metric correction has zero value and zero first derivative there. The base metric omega is unchanged and retains exactly the torsion terms proved in BK-1. Applying BK-1 coefficientwise therefore yields all four bundle identities at x_0. The point and frame were arbitrary, so the equalities are global operator identities.

proofs.title: The preliminary bundle Laplacian identity
proofs.statement: Delta''=Delta'+[iTheta,Lambda]+[C,tau*]-[B,sigma*].
proof: BK-2 gives b=-i[Lambda,C]-sigma*. Thus Delta''=[B,b]=-i[B,[Lambda,C]]-[B,sigma*]. By Jacobi, [B,[Lambda,C]]=[[B,Lambda],C]+[Lambda,[B,C]]. Since [B,Lambda]=i(a+tau*), and the bracket of two odd operators is symmetric, the first term is i[C,a+tau*]. The second is [Lambda,Theta]. Multiplication by -i converts them to [C,a]+[C,tau*]+[iTheta,Lambda]. This is the asserted formula. Each term has bidegree (0,0); in particular the final term uses sigma*, not tau*.

proofs.title: Combining the first-order torsion terms into a nonnegative square
proofs.statement: [L,tau]=3P, [Lambda,tau]=-2i sigma*, and -[B,sigma*]=[tau,a+tau*]+T, where T=[Lambda,[Lambda,(i/2)partial dbar omega wedge]]-[P,P*].
proof: Even exterior multiplication by omega commutes with P, and P raises total degree by three. Jacobi and BK-0 give [L,tau]=[L,[Lambda,P]]=[[L,Lambda],P]+[Lambda,[L,P]]=[H,P]=3P.

The identity [b,L]=i(C+tau) expresses tau=-i[b,L]-C. Also [B,L]=Q because the connection satisfies the graded Leibniz rule on a scalar even form; taking adjoints yields [Lambda,b]=Q*. Jacobi therefore gives [Lambda,[b,L]]=[Q*,L]+[b,-H]=sigma*-b: the first term is the adjoint of [Lambda,Q]=sigma, and [b,H]=b since b lowers degree by one. Substitute [Lambda,C]=i(b+sigma*) to obtain [Lambda,tau]=-i(sigma*-b)-i(b+sigma*)=-2i sigma*.

Set A_1=[B,Lambda]=i(a+tau*) and R=(dbar partial omega) wedge. The Leibniz rule on the odd scalar form partial omega gives [B,P]=R. Jacobi now yields [B,tau]=[A_1,P]+[Lambda,R] and [B,[Lambda,tau]]=[A_1,tau]+[Lambda,[B,tau]]. Substituting the first into the second and applying Jacobi once more produces [B,[Lambda,tau]]=[Lambda,[Lambda,R]]+2[tau,A_1]+[P,[Lambda,A_1]]. The factor 2 arises because both tau and A_1 are odd, so their bracket is symmetric; it is not discarded.

To evaluate the last bracket, [Lambda,A_1]=i[Lambda,a+tau*]=i[C+tau,L]*. Here [C,L]=P by the connection Leibniz rule, whereas [tau,L]=-3P by the first paragraph. Therefore [Lambda,A_1]=-2iP*. The preceding line becomes [Lambda,[Lambda,R]]+2i[tau,a+tau*]-2i[P,P*]. Since dbar partial omega=-partial dbar omega, its first term is 2i[Lambda,[Lambda,(i/2)partial dbar omega wedge]]. Finally sigma*=(i/2)[Lambda,tau] from the second paragraph, so multiplying by i/2 gives [B,sigma*]=-[tau,a+tau*]-T. This is the required torsion identity with every derivative order and factor retained.

proofs.title: The complete identity, energy inequality and exact receiver
proofs.statement: Delta''=Delta'_tau+[iTheta,Lambda]+T. For every compactly supported smooth E-valued (p,k)-form u, ||Bu||^2+||bu||^2>=integral <([iTheta,Lambda]+T)u,u>dV. This discharges the curvature input of WL-4, WL-5 and WL-6 for all the smooth weights and bundles used there.
proof: Insert BK-4 into BK-3. The terms Delta'+[C,tau*]+[tau,a+tau*] are exactly [C+tau,a+tau*] when expanded by bilinearity. This proves the operator identity. T is zero-order: all its factors are pointwise exterior multiplications or contractions; partial dbar omega differentiates the fixed metric coefficients, not u. Its coefficients are smooth and it depends only on omega. It acts on the bundle factor by the identity, so a scalar change of bundle weight leaves it unchanged.

The operator a+tau* is the actual formal adjoint of C+tau. For compactly supported u, integration by parts gives (Delta'_tau u,u)=||(C+tau)u||^2+||(a+tau*)u||^2>=0 and (Delta''u,u)=||Bu||^2+||bu||^2. Subtract the two in the proved identity to obtain the asserted exact energy equality with those two nonnegative squares, and then discard the squares for the inequality. Formal self-adjointness is sufficient; no spectral theorem or choice of self-adjoint extension is being assumed.

There is also no missing self-adjointness assumption on the pointwise curvature term. Apply the already-proved identity in a chart to the trivial line bundle with constant metric, for which Theta=0. T is the difference of two formally self-adjoint differential operators there. As a zero-order smooth operator it must therefore be pointwise self-adjoint: test its skew-adjoint part against arbitrary compactly supported vector functions and use continuity of its entries. For general E, the identity then shows that [iTheta,Lambda] is formally self-adjoint as well, hence pointwise self-adjoint because it too is zero-order. This justifies the operator inequalities and norms used in WL-3 without a further unproved fibrewise assertion.

Apply the theorem to the complete metric omega_tilde and the smooth bundle metric h exp(-Phi) of WL-0, WL-1, WL-2 and WL-3; nothing in BK-0 through BK-5 requires Kahlerness or compactness. For the twist F=K_M^(-1) tensor E, it applies to that holomorphic bundle itself, without trivializing K_M globally. The zero-order A_(Phi,k) is precisely [iTheta(F_Phi),Lambda]+T from WL-3. Thus the compact-support premise explicitly singled out in WL-4 is now supplied. WL-1 extends the resulting A>=Id estimate to the actual joint graph domain; WL-4 gives a smooth minimum-norm solution; and WL-5 and WL-6 give the full manifold vanishing and degree-(q-1) approximation, including their degree endpoints. This supplies the curvature hypothesis in those implications. Coherent-sheaf gluing and the proper-map finite-complex construction require the separate arguments CL-0 through QG-6 and FC-0 through FC-7.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Complex spaces are Hausdorff and second countable with their full coherent quotient structure sheaves. A local model i:A->Omega is a closed embedding defined by a coherent ideal J, with Omega open in C^N. The ideal is not replaced by its radical.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Fix an integer q>=1. Strong q-completeness means the existence of a smooth exhaustion, bounded below with compact sublevel closures, which is strongly q-convex everywhere in the ambient-extension sense of the QN package.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: For open U' contained in U, q-Runge completeness in this argument means: for each compact L contained in U', there are a smooth strongly q-convex exhaustion psi of U and a real b with L contained in {psi<b} and closure of {psi<b} compact in U'. This is the complete local version, not mere q-convexity outside a compact exceptional set.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: A coherent sheaf F has a distinguished patch A when i_*F admits a finite free resolution on Omega. Such patches form a local basis by the pinned programme providers. All sheaf maps below are O-linear before passing to cohomology; all cohomology maps are complex-linear and use quotient topologies, possibly non-Hausdorff.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Cech cochains use alternating indices, with C^r(W,F)=product over i_0<...<i_r of F(W_i0 intersect ... intersect W_ir). Empty intersections contribute zero. The differential is the alternating sum of restriction maps. Negative degrees of these ordinary complexes are zero.

proofs.title: Discharge of local coherent vanishing and the free-to-coherent lift
proofs.statement: Let A be a distinguished patch for F, with finite free ambient resolution 0->E_m->...->E_0->i_*F->0. If U is strongly q-complete and open in A, then H^k(U,F)=0 for k>=q. If V is any strongly q-complete ambient neighbourhood with A intersect V=U, the natural map H^(q-1)(V,E_0)->H^(q-1)(U,F) is surjective.
proof: The finite ambient resolution is the one in the pinned distinguished-patch provider, not a finite free resolution over the possibly singular or nonreduced ring O_A. Put Omega'=Omega minus (A minus U). Since A is closed in Omega and A minus U is closed in A, Omega' is open and U=A intersect Omega' is a full closed complex subspace of Omega'. QN-5 supplies a strongly q-complete neighbourhood V of U inside Omega'. Thus A intersect V=U, and restriction of the ambient resolution remains exact on V.

On this neighbourhood, WL-5, using the curvature identity BK-5, gives H^r(V,E_j)=0 for every r>=q and every finite free E_j. The exact dimension shift is as follows. Set K_-1=i_*F|V, and K_j=ker(E_j|V->K_(j-1)) for 0<=j<m; exactness identifies K_(m-1) with E_m|V. The sequence 0->K_j->E_j|V->K_(j-1)->0 gives H^r(V,K_(j-1)) isomorphic to H^(r+1)(V,K_j) for r>=q. Starting with the free final syzygy and descending in j kills every H^r(V,K_j), r>=q, including H^r(V,i_*F). When m=0, i_*F|V is already E_0|V and the same vanishing is immediate.

Exact closed pushforward gives H^r(V,i_*F|V)=H^r(U,F|U). For the lifting assertion, if m>=1, the tail resolution just considered gives H^q(V,K_0)=0. The connecting part H^(q-1)(V,E_0)->H^(q-1)(V,i_*F)->H^q(V,K_0) of the long exact sequence therefore makes the first arrow surjective. If m=0 this arrow is an isomorphism. Nothing here sets F equal to a sheaf on A_red: both the quotient ideal J and the actual O_A-module survive all restrictions and pushforwards. This proves local vanishing and the free-to-coherent lift. The global coherent dimension bound requires the additional gluing arguments ending in QG-6.

proofs.title: The cohomology topology and the precise open mapping argument
proofs.statement: Countable Stein-piece covers give a canonical quotient topology on coherent cohomology of a full complex space. Restrictions, coherent sheaf morphisms and closed-embedding cohomology comparisons are continuous. A surjection on cohomology induced by a continuous map of Frechet complexes is open, even when the cohomology spaces are not Hausdorff.
proof: By Frechet Propositions 5.1-5.2, F(W) has its canonical Frechet topology for every open W, and restriction and sheaf morphisms act continuously. Small chart balls intersected with full complex models give a countable Stein-piece basis. Finiteness Lemma 1.1 embeds each finite intersection as a closed complex subspace of a product of Stein manifolds; its graph ideal retains J and the equations of the other chart maps, rather than a radicalized ideal. Closed pushforward and Cartan B on that smooth product give vanishing of positive coherent cohomology on the intersection. Thus Corollary 1.2 makes the cover Leray on full complex spaces, not just manifolds.

For a countable such cover W, each C^r(W,F) is a countable product of Frechet spaces. The differential delta is continuous because each coordinate is a finite sum of continuous restrictions. Consequently Z^r=ker(delta:C^r->C^(r+1)) is a closed Frechet subspace. Give H^r=Z^r/delta C^(r-1) the quotient topology; no closedness of the denominator is asserted.

Here is the open-mapping mechanism used from Remark 2.3. Let rho:E^bullet->D^bullet be a continuous cochain map of Frechet complexes, inducing a surjection in degree r. Then T:Z^r(E) direct-sum D^(r-1)->Z^r(D), T(x,y)=rho(x)+d_D y, is continuous and surjective. Its domain and target are Frechet, so Theorem 1.1 makes T open. If W is open in H^r(E), its inverse image under pi_E:Z^r(E)->H^r(E) is open. The image T(pi_E^(-1)(W) times D^(r-1)) is exactly pi_D^(-1)(H^r(rho)(W)): equality follows by expressing equality of classes as a coboundary. Hence H^r(rho)(W) is quotient-open. This also proves that a cohomology bijection induced by rho is a homeomorphism. For r=0 the negative-degree summand is zero and the argument still applies.

Given two countable Stein-piece covers, choose a countable Stein-piece common refinement. A choice assigning each smaller open to a containing larger one induces a continuous cochain map by restriction, with alternating reordering and zero for repeated indices. Leray comparison makes its cohomology map the canonical bijection; the preceding paragraph makes it a homeomorphism. Thus the topology does not depend on the cover. For an open restriction or a coherent sheaf map, refine the relevant covers so that the actual cochain map consists of continuous section maps; its cohomology map is therefore continuous.

For a full closed embedding i:A->V choose a countable Stein open cover W of V. The intersections A intersect W_i are Stein pieces of A. On every multiple intersection, (i_*F)(W_I)=F(A intersect W_I). These equalities respect the canonical section topologies: locally both are quotients of the same ambient free-section space by the same relation module, and the global topologies are the closed compatible-family topologies of those local quotients. Therefore the two Cech complexes are degreewise identical as topological complexes. This realizes H^r(V,i_*F)=H^r(A,F) as a topological isomorphism and verifies its compatibility with restriction. No continuous linear splitting of any quotient is claimed.

proofs.title: Transport from smooth-form approximation to the Cech quotient topology
proofs.statement: On an open subset V of C^N, the Dolbeault and Cech realizations of H^r(V,O^p) are topologically isomorphic for the natural quotient topologies, and this comparison commutes with restriction to open subsets.
proof: Choose a countable locally finite cover W of V by sufficiently small Stein opens and a smooth locally finite partition (theta_i) subordinate to it, with supports closed in V and contained in W_i. Such a cover and partition are available from the smooth partition provider already used in Dolbeault Lemma 3.1. Form D^(a,b)=product over increasing (a+1)-tuples I of smooth C^p-valued (0,b)-forms on W_I. With delta the Cech differential and dbar acting on coefficients, restriction implies delta dbar=dbar delta. Set the total differential on D^(a,b) to delta+(-1)^a dbar. The mixed terms have opposite signs, so its square is zero. Each total degree is a finite direct sum of Frechet spaces.

There are continuous cochain maps j:Gamma(V,E^(0,bullet) tensor C^p)->Tot(D), given by restriction into column a=0, and k:C^bullet(W,O^p)->Tot(D), given by inclusion into row b=0. For the horizontal rows, the operation (hc)_I=sum_j theta_j c_(jI) gives the augmented Cech contraction delta h+h delta=identity, as in Dolbeault Lemma 3.1. Multiplication is extended by zero outside W_j. It is continuous: on a compact set in an output intersection, only finitely many supports meet that compact set, and each required derivative is controlled by finitely many input seminorms on compact subsets of the corresponding W_j intersect W_I.

The map j is a quasi-isomorphism by finite diagonal elimination, which can be seen without an infinite spectral-sequence limit. For a total cocycle of degree r, its component with largest positive horizontal degree a is delta-closed by the total cocycle equation. Subtract the total differential of its horizontal primitive, using h, to remove that component. The subtraction creates components only in smaller horizontal degree. Repeat until only column a=0 remains. That column is horizontally closed, hence glues to a global form, and the remaining total equation says the global form is dbar-closed. If such a global closed form is a total boundary, apply the same elimination to its total primitive; all components of positive horizontal degree can be removed without changing its total differential. What remains is a global primitive. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity for j.

For k use vertical elimination. Every W_I is Stein and H^b(W_I,O^p)=0 for b>0, by the pinned Stein and Dolbeault providers. Thus each column has cohomology O(W_I)^p in degree zero and none above. Given a total cocycle, its component with smallest horizontal degree a and positive vertical degree b is dbar-closed. Choose a vertical primitive on each W_I and subtract its total differential, inserting the sign (-1)^a in the primitive. This removes that component and can create one only in the next horizontal degree. Repetition terminates on this finite diagonal at b=0, where the remaining entries are holomorphic Cech cocycles. The identical elimination applied to a primitive of a boundary proves injectivity. No continuous choice of vertical primitives is needed for this algebraic quasi-isomorphism.

Both j and k are continuous maps of Frechet complexes and induce cohomology bijections. CL-1 therefore makes both induced maps homeomorphisms, even if their boundary subspaces are not closed. The resulting comparison is the usual Dolbeault identification from the two resolutions. To check restrictions, compare covers using a common subordinate cover on the smaller open set: all inclusions into the double complex and all restriction maps commute before taking cohomology. Refinement comparisons from CL-1 then give the canonical commuting restriction square. Consequently the C-infinity-local approximation of closed forms in WL-6 yields density in the Cech quotient topology used in CL-1; no unproved identification of topologies is being inserted.

proofs.title: Ambient sublevels with a strict, quantified margin
proofs.statement: Let U' be q-Runge complete in U inside a distinguished patch A. For each compact L in U', there are a strongly q-complete ambient open V with A intersect V=U, a strongly q-convex exhaustion h of V, and c such that L is contained in U_c=A intersect {h<c}, whose closure is compact in U'. Both V and V_c={h<c} are strongly q-complete.
proof: If U' is empty, all its cohomology groups are zero and the final approximation theorem is immediate. Otherwise an empty compact L can be enlarged by one point of U'. Choose the exhaustion psi and level b supplied by the definition for the resulting nonempty compact L. Put a=max_L psi, epsilon=(b-a)/3 and c=b-epsilon. These satisfy a+epsilon<c<b.

Use Omega'=Omega minus (A minus U), so U is closed in Omega'. The proof of QN-5 works with arbitrary constant upper margin epsilon: apply QN-3 with delta=epsilon instead of 1; all remaining steps are unchanged, and the resulting h equals its extended function phi near U. Thus obtain a strongly q-complete neighbourhood V of U inside Omega' with psi<=h|U<psi+epsilon. For x in L, h(x)<a+epsilon<c. For x in U_c, psi(x)<=h(x)<c<b. Since {psi<=c} is compact and contained in {psi<b}, the closure of U_c is compact in U'. Importantly, V contains all of U, whereas only its selected sublevel cuts out U_c inside U'; it is not asserted that U'=A intersect V.

The function t->1/(c-t) on (-infinity,c) has positive first and second derivatives. Hence 1/(c-h) is strongly q-convex on V_c: its Levi form retains a positive multiple of the same positive subspace as the Levi form of h and adds a nonnegative rank-one term. Its sublevels are contained in compact h-sublevels strictly below c, and are closed there, so it is an exhaustion of V_c. For any compact K in V_c, choose max_K h<b_0<b_1<c. The h-sublevels at b_0 and b_1 then have compact closures nested inside V_c. This checks exactly the q-Runge hypothesis needed by WL-6 for V_c inside V, including its two inner levels. Restricting the original finite ambient free resolution to these opens preserves its exactness.

proofs.title: Dense coherent restriction at each selected sublevel
proofs.statement: For the opens in CL-3 and r=q-1, the restriction H^r(U,F)->H^r(U_c,F) has dense image in the canonical quotient topology.
proof: Let E_0=O^p be the initial free module in the fixed ambient resolution. Form the square with top row H^r(V,E_0)->H^r(U,F), bottom row H^r(V_c,E_0)->H^r(U_c,F), and vertical arrows given by restriction. Closed-embedding identifications in CL-1 identify these rows with the maps induced by E_0->i_*F. The square commutes by functoriality of restriction. The two horizontal arrows are surjective by CL-0 applied on V and V_c, using the tails of the same restricted resolution. All arrows are continuous by CL-1; the horizontal surjections are also open, although their openness is not needed for the following density argument.

The left restriction has dense image: represent a class in H^r(V_c,E_0) by a closed smooth form, apply WL-6 using the verified inner levels from CL-3, and pass through the topological comparisons of CL-2. The WL degree endpoints q>N are included in that existing proof, so there is no new dimension restriction here.

To prove density on the right, take a nonempty open set O in H^r(U_c,F). Surjectivity of the bottom horizontal map makes its inverse image nonempty, and continuity makes that inverse image open. Density on the left gives a class from H^r(V,E_0) whose restriction lies in that inverse image. Its image along the top row is a class on U restricting into O. This argument uses neither Hausdorffness of cohomology nor a splitting of the coherent quotient.

proofs.title: Exhaustion, exact cochain lifting, and local coherent approximation
proofs.statement: Under the hypotheses of CL-3, H^(q-1)(U,F)->H^(q-1)(U',F) has dense image. In a common countable Stein-piece model, the restrictions of cocycles from U are already dense in the cocycle space over U'.
proof: Choose compact sets K_n exhausting U', with their interiors covering U'. Apply CL-3 inductively, including K_n and the compact closure of the preceding chosen open in the next compact set. This gives opens U_n with closure(U_n) contained in U_(n+1), each closure compact in U', and union U_n=U'. The ambient V and exhaustion h can vary with n; CL-4 applies to every resulting restriction from the fixed U to U_n. No common ambient exhaustion for all n is assumed.

Choose a countable basis W of relatively compact Stein pieces in U, small enough to lie in distinguished patches for F. Let W' be the subfamily with compact closure in U', and W_n the subfamily with compact closure in U_n. These are Leray covers of U', U_n; W covers U. The W_n are nested and their union is W': the compact closure of any member of W' is covered by the nested U_n and is contained in one of them. Put P^bullet=C^bullet(W,F), E^bullet=C^bullet(W',F), and E_n^bullet=C^bullet(W_n,F). Every projection P^r->E_n^r and E_(n+1)^r->E_n^r simply forgets factors, and is surjective. A cochain can be extended by setting the missing coordinates to zero. This is only a degreewise lift: zero extension need not commute with delta and must not be used to lift cocycles.

There is a degreewise topological isomorphism E^bullet=lim_n E_n^bullet. Every finite tuple of indices in W' lies entirely in some W_n; compatible families therefore specify exactly all the coordinates of E. A basic product neighbourhood involves only finitely many coordinates and finitely many seminorms on them, all visible at one such n, which proves the topological assertion. The differentials agree because their coordinate formulas use finitely many restrictions. This identifies complexes, not cohomology with an inverse limit of cohomology groups.

Set r=q-1 and let z be a cocycle of E. Given a basic neighbourhood of z in Z^r(E), choose n large enough to contain all its tested coordinates, and choose a zero-neighbourhood N in Z^r(E_n) whose pullback is inside that neighbourhood translated by -z. The quotient map pi_n:Z^r(E_n)->H^r(E_n) is open: the saturation of any open set is the union of its translates by coboundaries. By CL-4, H^r(P)->H^r(E_n) has dense image. Hence there is x in Z^r(P) with [x_n] in pi_n(z_n+N). Equivalently z_n-x_n-delta a is in N after replacing N by a symmetric smaller zero-neighbourhood if necessary, for some a in E_n^(r-1).

If r>=1, use degreewise surjectivity to choose b in P^(r-1) with b_n=a, and put x'=x+delta b. Then delta x'=0 because delta x=0 and delta^2=0; moreover z_n-x'_n=z_n-x_n-delta a lies in N. Thus the restriction of x' to E lies in the prescribed neighbourhood of z. If r=0 there are no coboundaries or negative-degree cochains, and the same argument works with a=b=0. This proves density of Z^r(P)->Z^r(E), and passage to quotient gives the stated density of H^r(U,F)->H^r(U',F). It is the concrete coordinate-surjective case of the already supplied Frechet Proposition 3.1(4), with its lifting hypotheses now checked on the actual complexes.

If desired, a convergent sequence of cocycles is obtained by applying the preceding construction to a decreasing countable neighbourhood basis at z. The cocycle space is Frechet, so it is first countable. This does not require cohomology itself to be Hausdorff. The proof retains F and every original nilpotent or torsion direction throughout. It proves the local approximation lemma only: global q-bump comparison, its connecting-map continuity, the final global inverse-limit vanishing, and the separate relative finite-complex theorem are not concluded from it.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: All complex spaces are Hausdorff and countable at infinity as in the bound programme providers. The structure sheaf may have nilpotents. F denotes a coherent module for that full structure sheaf; no radicalization of F or of its local defining ideal is performed.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Fix an integer q>=1. Strong q-convexity means that locally a smooth real function has an ambient smooth extension whose Levi form has at least N-q+1 positive directions in ambient dimension N. When N<q the requirement is vacuous. Geometry on the reduced support is transferred by the local-embedding comparison QN-0; this does not replace coherent coefficients by their reduction.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: An exhaustion is bounded below and has compact closed sublevel sets. Write X_t={psi<t}. A q-Runge-complete open W in U has the following property: each compact L in W lies inside a sublevel {h<b} compactly contained in W for some strongly q-convex exhaustion h of U.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Use alternating ordered Cech cochains, with zero on repeated indices and delta c at an increasing tuple equal to the alternating sum of restrictions after deletion of one index. Negative cochain degrees are zero. Cohomology carries the quotient topology on cocycles modulo coboundaries. It need not be Hausdorff before QG-3.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Every cochain map below is continuous and complex-linear. Global cohomology is not assigned an O(X)-module structure stronger than the natural compatible one without specifying the underlying ring; the topological arguments need only complex-linearity.

proofs.title: A Frechet model of the two-open Mayer-Vietoris sequence
proofs.statement: For T=G union U and W=G intersect U, construct topological cochain models giving the Mayer-Vietoris sequence for coherent F. In these models the connecting map is induced by a continuous shifted inclusion, without assuming closed coboundary spaces.
proof: Choose countable Stein-piece covers (G_i) indexed by I and (U_j) indexed by J. Each piece is an open subset of T contained in the indicated side. Every finite intersection is coherent-acyclic by the imported full-space intersection lemma. Order all I indices before all J indices, retaining an order within each set. Let P=C(G_i,F), Q=C(U_j,F), and C=C((G_i),(U_j);F). All three are nonnegative Frechet complexes: each degree is a countable product of section Frechet spaces, with a continuous finite-coordinate differential. They compute H(G,F), H(U,F), and H(T,F), respectively.

Introduce the double complex R^(a,b)=product F(G_(i0...ia) intersect U_(j0...jb)) for a,b>=0, with differential d_R=delta_G+(-1)^a delta_U. Its total degree is a+b; the direct sum in each total degree is finite. Restriction of a pure G cochain to intersections with each U_j defines a continuous cochain map j_G:P->Tot R in row b=0. Likewise j_U:Q->Tot R occupies column a=0. The unused differential annihilates these restrictions because two successive restrictions agree. Put rho(p,u)=j_U(u)-j_G(p).

A mixed cochain in C^n has a+1 G indices and b+1 U indices, where a+b=n-1. Multiply its coordinate by (-1)^a and call the resulting element r of (Tot R)^(n-1). This produces a degreewise topological isomorphism C^n=P^n direct-sum Q^n direct-sum (Tot R)^(n-1). Under it the differential is D(p,u,r)=(d_P p,d_Q u,rho(p,u)-d_R r). To check the signs, deletion of a G index in a mixed tuple changes a by one, producing -delta_G after conjugation. Deletion of a U index contributes (-1)^(a+1), producing -(-1)^a delta_U. At an edge with only one U index, deleting it sends a pure G cochain to -j_G(p); at the edge with only one G index it sends a pure U cochain to j_U(u). These formulas include the n=0 edge, whose mixed degree is -1 and is zero.

Since rho is a cochain map, D^2=0: the mixed component of D^2 is rho(d_P p,d_Q u)-d_R rho(p,u)+d_R^2 r=0. Projection C->P direct-sum Q and inclusion (Tot R)[-1]->C, r->(0,0,r), form a degreewise split short exact sequence of topological vector spaces. The shifted differential on (Tot R)[-1] is -d_R. The splitting is only degreewise; no false cochain splitting is asserted.

The resulting long exact sequence contains H^k(C)->H^k(P) direct-sum H^k(Q) --H(rho)--> H^k(Tot R) --partial--> H^(k+1)(C).
