This can be checked directly: a closed pair (p,u) lifts to a cocycle of C exactly when rho(p,u)=d_R r; a closed mixed z maps to a boundary exactly when its class is the rho image of a closed pair. The kernel of projection on H(C) consists of mixed classes after subtracting a boundary lifting any exact pure components. These are the three exactness assertions and repeat in each degree.

In this convention partial sends [z] to [(0,0,z)]. The linear map Z^k(Tot R)->Z^(k+1)(C) used here is continuous. A boundary z=d_R w maps to D(0,0,-w), so the map descends continuously to the quotient cohomology spaces. This proves continuity of the connecting map directly; it is not a restriction map. Identification of H(Tot R) with the canonical H(W,F), including topology and natural restrictions, is supplied next.

proofs.title: Topological comparison for the mixed overlap complex
proofs.statement: The complex Tot R in QG-0 computes H(W,F) with its canonical quotient topology, and j_G and j_U induce the ordinary restriction maps. Thus all Mayer-Vietoris maps in QG-0 are continuous in the canonical coherent-cohomology topologies.
proof: Cover W by D_(i,j)=G_i intersect U_j, retaining empty members as zero factors if convenient. This countable cover and all its finite intersections consist of Stein pieces, so its Cech complex A=C(D,F) computes H(W,F). Form the triple complex T^(a,b,c)=product F(G_I intersect U_J intersect D_K), with increasing nonempty I,J,K of lengths a+1,b+1,c+1. Its total differential is delta_G+(-1)^a delta_U+(-1)^(a+b) delta_D. Restriction gives continuous augmentations Tot R->Tot T and A->Tot T, the latter occupying a=b=0. They are cochain maps because the newly introduced Cech differentials of an augmented section are zero.

For fixed I,J, the cover by D_(i,j) restricted to G_I intersect U_J contains that whole open set as a member: choose the first i in I and the first j in J. Consequently its augmented Cech complex, starting with F(G_I intersect U_J), is contractible. Explicitly extend cochains alternately to all ordered tuples and insert that chosen member as the first index; restriction to the other indices then gives h delta+delta h=identity, with the augmentation included. Repeated indices give zero. All restrictions and insertions are continuous.

For fixed K, the intersection D_K is contained in G_i and U_j for the first pair (i,j) in K. Thus the G cover restricted to D_K, and then the U cover restricted to D_K, each contain the entire set as a member. The same insertion homotopy makes both augmented directions exact. This proves exactness without selecting holomorphic splittings or assuming cohomology is Hausdorff.

These exact augmented directions prove both augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. One explicit total-complex argument is to remove a component in the highest positive augmented direction by subtracting the total differential of its insertion-homotopy preimage; the cycle equation makes the component closed in that direction. The subtraction removes it and can move components only one step toward the next direction. Repeat until the augmented degree is zero, where the remaining kernel is precisely the augmented section. Apply the same elimination to a total boundary to prove injectivity. For the second map eliminate the G and U augmented directions successively. In total degree n there are only finitely many triples a+b+c=n, so the algorithm terminates. The chosen insertions need not commute with the other differential; those discrepancies are precisely the lower-direction components removed at the next step.

Each augmentation is a continuous map of Frechet complexes. CL-1 therefore turns its algebraic cohomology isomorphism into a homeomorphism, by applying the Frechet open mapping theorem to the map from source cocycles plus target lower-degree cochains onto target cocycles. The common identification H(Tot R)=H(A)=H(W,F) is consequently topological even when these spaces are non-Hausdorff. The augmentations agree on an ordinary section and all their coordinates are restrictions. Composing the G or U cover comparison through this common refinement consequently gives exactly restriction to W, not a different abstract isomorphism. QG-0 is the canonical two-open sequence with the stated sign convention for its difference and connecting maps.

proofs.title: Finite q-convex bumps with common positive Levi directions
proofs.statement: Let psi be a smooth exhaustion of X, strongly q-convex off compact K. If K is contained in X_c and d>c, the inclusion X_c subset X_d factors into finitely many G_j subset G_(j+1)=G_j union U_j. Each G_j is a global sublevel of such an exhaustion with the same exceptional compact K. Each U_j lies in a distinguished patch for F, and U_j and W_j=G_j intersect U_j are strongly q-complete; W_j is q-Runge-complete in U_j.
proof: The closed band B={c<=psi<=d} is compact and avoids K. Cover it by finitely many distinguished patches A_j, each a full closed analytic subspace of a Euclidean ball Omega_j=B(z_j,r_j), with a finite ambient free resolution of F on a slightly larger ball. Shrink these patches inside charts on which psi has a strongly q-convex ambient extension; arrange their closures to avoid K. QN-1 gives smooth theta_j>=0, with compact support in A_j, sum theta_j<=1 everywhere, and sum theta_j=1 on a neighbourhood of B. For example take a finite partition on a neighbourhood of B and multiply it by a cutoff supported in that neighbourhood and equal to one near B.

Fix finitely many common ambient charts covering the union of those supports and the closures of the small patch balls. On a smaller chart, the Levi form of psi is positive on a fixed subspace with a uniform strictly positive lower bound, by continuity; QN-0 permits use of one ambient embedding. The finitely many theta_k have ambient extensions with bounded second derivatives on these compact chart closures. Choose epsilon_0>0 so the sum of the perturbation norms, multiplied by epsilon_0, is below half every required positive lower bound. Then, for every partial sum and alpha in [0,1], psi-epsilon sum_(k<j)theta_k-alpha epsilon theta_j is positive on the SAME chosen subspace when 0<epsilon<=epsilon_0. Outside the compact supports there is no change. In charts of dimension less than q the required index condition is empty. This establishes common directions, not merely separate q-convexity of two functions.

For t in [c,d) and epsilon<=min(epsilon_0,d-t), put psi_j=psi-epsilon sum_(k<j)theta_k and G_j={psi_j<t}. All psi_j are bounded below proper exhaustions: their difference from psi is bounded and has compact support. They agree with psi near K. The sets G_j increase, G_0=X_t and G_s=X_(t+epsilon). For the last equality, points with psi<t are in both; in the band t<=psi<t+epsilon the full sum equals one; and when psi>=t+epsilon the inequality sum theta<=1 prevents entry into G_s. Since psi_(j+1)-psi_j is supported in A_j, putting U_j=A_j intersect G_(j+1) gives G_(j+1)=G_j union U_j and W_j=A_j intersect G_j.

On U_j use phi_j=1/(t-psi_(j+1))+1/(r_j^2-|z-z_j|^2), restricting the indicated ambient functions to A_j. On W_j use the analogous formula with psi_j in the first denominator. Both denominators are positive. For f(s)=1/(t-s), f'>0 and f''>0 on s<t. Its Levi form is f'(psi)H_psi plus the nonnegative rank-one gradient term. The radial reciprocal is strictly plurisubharmonic. Thus the chosen positive subspaces remain positive, proving strong q-convexity. A bounded sublevel keeps both denominators bounded away from zero and z inside a smaller closed ball. Closedness of the analytic model then makes that sublevel compact within U_j, or within W_j respectively. Hence these functions are exhaustions.

Given nonempty compact L in W_j, let a=max_L psi_j and choose b with a<b<t. On U_j put h_eta=psi_j+eta phi_j for eta>0. The function psi_j has a global lower bound, while phi_j is nonnegative and proper, so h_eta is a bounded-below exhaustion. Its Levi form is the Levi form of psi_j plus a positive multiple of H_(psi_(j+1)), nonnegative gradient terms and a positive radial term. The common positive directions fixed above therefore prove strong q-convexity. Choose eta so that eta max_L phi_j<b-a. Then L subset {h_eta<b}; also psi_j<=h_eta, so its closure lies in {psi_j<=b}, strictly inside W_j. Since h_eta is proper, that closure is compact in U_j and hence compact in W_j. This is the required q-Runge witness. Empty L is automatic if W_j is nonempty by choosing any such witness; if W_j is empty all its cohomology and approximation requirements are trivial.

Choose a finite partition c=t_0<...<t_N=d with increments at most epsilon_0 and repeat the same finite-cutoff construction for each adjacent pair. The estimates were uniform on the original compact band. Concatenating the finite lists proves the assertion for X_c subset X_d. No smoothness of the boundary levels, regular-value theorem, reducedness of the structure sheaf, or closure of arbitrary sums of q-convex functions is used.

proofs.title: Coarse sublevel comparison and noncircular finiteness
proofs.statement: Under the hypotheses of QG-2, restriction H^k(X_d,F)->H^k(X_c,F) is surjective for k=q and bijective for k>q. For every c with K subset X_c and every k>=q, H^k(X_c,F) is finite-dimensional and Hausdorff. This conclusion does not use density or injectivity in degree q.
proof: For one bump put T=G union U and W=G intersect U as in QG-2. CL-0 applies on the same distinguished ambient patch to both U and W and gives H^k(U,F)=H^k(W,F)=0 for k>=q. In the exact sequence of QG-0, the zero group H^k(W,F) implies surjectivity of H^k(T,F)->H^k(G,F) for k>=q. If k>q, the preceding H^(k-1)(W,F) also vanishes, proving injectivity. Compose these maps over the finite list of bumps. No topological conclusion about any cohomology group has been used here.

Fix c and choose d>c. The closure of X_c is compact and lies in X_d. Choose a countable Stein-piece cover V=(V_i) of X_d and a finite family of shrunk open sets V'_ell compactly contained in selected V_(a(ell)), covering the closure of X_c. Choose a countable Stein-piece cover W of X_c refining (V'_ell intersect X_c). All endpoint covers are Leray by the imported intersection lemma; the intermediate finite cover is not asserted to be Leray. The refinement maps define a continuous cochain map C(V,F)->C((V'_ell intersect X_c),F)->C(W,F), which induces ordinary restriction on sheaf cohomology.

In each fixed cochain degree the first target is a finite product. Its component maps restrict F(V_(a(ell_0)) intersect ... intersect V_(a(ell_k))) to F(V'_ell_0 intersect ... intersect V'_ell_k intersect X_c), with the alternating sign determined by index order; repeated source indices give zero. The latter open has compact closure inside the former, because each closure(V'_ell) is compact in its assigned V_(a(ell)). Proposition 5.2(3) of the Frechet provider makes each nonzero component compact. Only finitely many source coordinates are used. The intersection of their witnessing zero-neighbourhoods is a zero-neighbourhood in the source product, whose image has compact closure in the finite target product. Thus the first map is compact in each degree. Composition with the continuous second refinement remains compact, even though its target can have infinitely many factors.

The cohomology map of this compact cochain map is surjective in degree k>=q by the coarse comparison already proved. Apply the bound Schwartz finiteness criterion to the two endpoint Frechet complexes. It shows that the target coboundaries are closed in the cocycles and that H^k(X_c,F) is finite-dimensional. The quotient topology of CL-1 is therefore Hausdorff. This proof applies to any smooth exhaustion strongly q-convex outside its compact exceptional set. In particular each intermediate G_j of QG-2 is a permitted target: its defining psi_j is such an exhaustion, and its level contains K. Hence H^q(G_j,F) is Hausdorff before QG-4 uses any dense image.

proofs.title: Sharp sublevel comparison and approximation in the boundary degree
proofs.statement: For K subset X_c and d>c, restriction H^k(X_d,F)->H^k(X_c,F) is a topological isomorphism for k>=q and has dense image for k=q-1. The density assertion does not require H^(q-1) to be Hausdorff.
proof: Consider a single bump T=G union U and W=G intersect U. By CL-5 and QG-2, the map H^(q-1)(U,F)->H^(q-1)(W,F) has dense image. Exactness makes its composite with partial:H^(q-1)(W,F)->H^q(T,F) zero. QG-0 and QG-1 prove partial continuous, while QG-3 proves H^q(T,F) Hausdorff. The kernel of partial is consequently closed and contains a dense subset, so partial=0. Exactness now makes H^q(T,F)->H^q(G,F) injective, supplementing the surjectivity from QG-3. In degrees greater than q bijectivity was already proved. These restrictions are induced by continuous Frechet cochain maps; CL-1 makes their cohomology bijections homeomorphisms.

Put r=q-1. The now-zero connecting map also makes rho:H^r(G,F) direct-sum H^r(U,F)->H^r(W,F), rho(g,u)=u|W-g|W, surjective. This map is induced by the continuous cochain map P direct-sum Q->Tot R of QG-0. CL-1 and the topological identification QG-1 therefore make rho open. This is an application of the Frechet open mapping theorem on cocycles plus lower-degree cochains, not an assumption that these possibly non-Hausdorff cohomology spaces themselves are Frechet.

To prove density of restriction from T to G, fix g in H^r(G,F) and an open neighbourhood O of g. Choose a symmetric zero-neighbourhood V with g-V subset O, and any zero-neighbourhood N in H^r(U,F). Openness makes rho(V direct-sum N) an open zero-neighbourhood in H^r(W,F). Since restrictions from U are dense, there is u with rho(g,u)=u|W-g|W in this neighbourhood. Choose (g',u') in V direct-sum N whose rho image is rho(g,u). Then rho(g-g',u-u')=0. Exactness supplies a class f in H^r(T,F) restricting to g-g' on G and u-u' on U. Its G restriction belongs to O. This proves density without a continuous splitting, without chosen lifts of an entire convergent sequence, and without Hausdorffness of H^r.

A finite composite of continuous maps with dense image again has dense image: continuity puts the image of the closure of a set inside the closure of its image, and the intermediate image is dense in the next target. Apply this to the bump factorization. The topological isomorphisms in higher degrees compose as well. This proves both conclusions for X_d->X_c. For q=1 the argument uses r=0; the negative cochain groups in the open-mapping construction are zero, so no exceptional negative-degree term has been assumed.

proofs.title: Global coherent vanishing by a cochain exhaustion limit
proofs.statement: If X admits a smooth strongly q-convex exhaustion everywhere, then H^k(X,F)=0 for every coherent F and every k>=q, including nonreduced full complex spaces.
proof: Set K=empty. Choose c below the lower bound of the exhaustion psi. Then X_c is empty. For each d>c, QG-4 identifies H^k(X_d,F) with H^k(X_c,F)=0 for k>=q. Hence every finite sublevel has the claimed vanishing. This does not by itself imply vanishing on the union; the following cochain argument supplies the missing step.

Take a countable basis W of relatively compact Stein pieces of X, subordinate to distinguished patches for F. Let W_n consist of those basis members whose compact closures lie in X_(c+n), for n>=0. These subfamilies cover the respective sublevels, are nested and have union W. Indeed any basis member has compact closure in X and the increasing sublevels eventually contain that closure. Define E_n=C(W_n,F). Each is a Frechet complex computing the corresponding coherent cohomology, and every degree of E_(n+1)->E_n is the coordinate projection that forgets tuples involving new indices. It is surjective: extend a cochain by zero on those tuples. Zero extension is NOT claimed to preserve cocycles or commute with the differential.

The complex E=C(W,F) is the topological inverse limit of the E_n. Each finite tuple of indices occurs at one finite stage, so a compatible inverse-limit element specifies exactly its section coordinate. Each basic product neighbourhood involves finitely many coordinates and finitely many seminorms and is therefore detected at some stage. These two facts prove the algebraic and topological identification degreewise. The differentials also agree coordinatewise. No commutation of cohomology with inverse limits has been inferred.

Fix k>=q. The transition maps on H^k(E_n) are injective because both groups are zero. The transitions on H^(k-1)(E_n) have dense image: for k=q this is QG-4, and for k>q both groups are zero. Together with degreewise surjectivity, these verify the hypotheses of the imported Frechet Proposition 3.1(3), which makes H^k(E)->H^k(E_0)=0 injective. Here is its needed special case explicitly, to show how the exact projection maps are used.

Let x be a closed degree-k cochain of E. Write x_n for its projection. Since H^k(E_n)=0, choose y_n in E_n^(k-1) with d y_n=x_n. Cocycles of degree k-1 from E_(n+1) have dense image among cocycles of E_n: density on quotient cohomology lets one approximate a target cocycle by a restricted cocycle plus d b with b in E_n^(k-2), and surjectivity in degree k-2 lifts b to E_(n+1), absorbing that coboundary into the approximating cocycle. If k=1, there is no degree -1 and no coboundary to absorb; H^0=Z^0, so the assertion is the given density directly.

Choose complete translation-invariant metrics on the degree-(k-1) spaces, successively enlarged by the finitely many pullbacks of earlier metrics so that every projection has Lipschitz constant at most one. Having chosen y_n, choose any primitive v in E_(n+1)^(k-1) for x_(n+1). The difference v|n-y_n is a cocycle. By the just-proved density, subtract a cocycle z from v so the new primitive y_(n+1)=v-z satisfies d_n(y_(n+1)|n,y_n)<2^(-n). This subtraction leaves d y_(n+1)=x_(n+1). For each fixed stage m, the projected primitives form a Cauchy sequence, because the tail distances are bounded by the summable series of these errors. Completeness gives a limit y^m. Continuity of all projections makes the limits compatible, and continuity of d gives d y^m=x_m. They thus define y in E^(k-1) with d y=x. This proves vanishing directly.

All terms throughout are sections of the original F on the full complex space. The geometry determines which open subsets are used but never passes cohomology to reduced coefficients. The conclusion is the full strongly q-complete coherent vanishing theorem needed for the compact-fibre deduction. It does not prove that every noncompact n-dimensional space has the particular exhaustion required by a separate general dimension theorem.

proofs.title: Compact analytic dimension bound with full coherent coefficients
proofs.statement: For a compact complex analytic space Z with dim Z<=n and any coherent O_Z-module F, H^k(Z,F)=0 when k>n. In particular this supplies the exact dimension-two full-fibre input retained for S6, without assuming smooth or reduced fibres.
proof: First construct a strongly (n+1)-convex smooth function on the reduced support of Z by induction on dimension. The empty case is immediate. In dimension zero the compact support is a finite discrete set. The constant zero function has, near each point, the ambient extension |z|^2 after centering coordinates at that point, so it is strongly 1-convex. Every continuous function on this finite compact support is an exhaustion under the bounded-below compact-sublevel convention.

For the induction step, the finite analytic stratification of QN-1 gives a compact analytic subset Y of dimension at most n-1 whose complement in Z_red is a smooth manifold of pure dimension n: take the singular locus together with all lower-dimensional components. If the whole space has smaller dimension, the preceding induction statement already applies and strong (n+1)-convexity follows from the stronger lower-index property. Otherwise apply induction to Y. It has a strongly n-convex exhaustion, since any stronger index obtained in lower dimension also meets the n-convex condition.

If Y is nonempty, QN-5 supplies an open neighbourhood V of Y in Z_red and a strongly n-convex smooth exhaustion phi of V. By compactness of Y and QN-1, choose a smooth cutoff eta supported compactly inside V and equal to one on a neighbourhood of Y. Set h=eta phi on V and h=0 outside the support. Because the support stays inside V this is globally smooth. Near Y it equals phi and is strongly n-convex, hence strongly (n+1)-convex. At every point outside Y the space is a smooth n-manifold; strong (n+1)-convexity is vacuous in its intrinsic n-dimensional chart. QN-0 transfers that property to any larger ambient embedding. If Y is empty simply use h=0 on the smooth n-manifold. In either case h is strongly (n+1)-convex everywhere and is a bounded-below exhaustion by compactness of Z.

Smooth real functions and their Levi index on a full analytic space are defined on its support by local ambient extensions. Consequently the function just constructed also supplies strong (n+1)-completeness for the original full Z. This step transfers geometric data only: O_Z, its possibly nonradical local ideal, and F are unchanged. Apply QG-5 on this full space with q=n+1. It gives H^k(Z,F)=0 for k>=n+1, which is the claimed dimension bound. The deduction uses the neighbourhood construction QN-5 and the global vanishing theorem QG-5, with the full coherent coefficients unchanged.

For the retained S6 map f:X->B, properness makes the support of each full fibre Z=X_b compact, and its assigned pure dimension is two. The restricted coefficient E|Z=E tensor_(O_X) O_Z is a coherent, indeed locally free, O_Z-module. Apply the proved result with n=2 to obtain H^k(X_b,E|X_b)=0 for all k>2. Flatness is not needed for this fibrewise vanishing lemma; it remains a hypothesis of the separate proper-flat relative-complex and base-change argument. No compactness of X, smoothness or reducedness of a fibre, constant h^2, or locally free higher direct image has been introduced.

Fibrewise vanishing alone does not assert R^k f_*E=0 or identify the canonical base-change map. Those conclusions still require the retained general relative finite-complex construction and its canonical derived-fibre comparison, together with the previously recorded algebraic deduction. The general noncompact dimension theorem and the source's separate top-degree conclusions remain outside this compact-fibre proof; they are neither declared false nor silently discarded.

chapters.title: Completed tensors and nuclear coherent sections

conventions.label: seminorm_completion
conventions.text: E_p is the Banach completion of E/ker(p), not E with an assumed complete p-norm. An increasing defining sequence (p_j) gives continuous maps E_(j+1) -> E_j.

conventions.label: completed_tensors
conventions.text: hat_pi and hat_epsilon denote Hausdorff completions for the projective and injective tensor seminorms. hat_tensor without a suffix is used only after NS-3 proves the two topologies coincide in the case at hand.

conventions.label: exact_sequence
conventions.text: In a short exact sequence of Frechet spaces the first map identifies a closed subspace and the last map is an open surjection. These topological properties follow from the open mapping theorem when the sequence is algebraically exact and its maps are continuous.

conventions.label: nuclear_map
conventions.text: A map T:E -> F is nuclear when T(x)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(x)y_j, with sum_j |lambda_j| finite, (xi_j) equicontinuous in E', and (y_j) bounded in F. This is a representation, not an asserted unique tensor for T.

conventions.label: nuclear_space
conventions.text: E is nuclear if it has an increasing defining sequence p_j for which E_(j+1) -> E_j is a nuclear Banach-space map for every j.

conventions.label: external_product
conventions.text: F boxtimes G on X x Y means pr_X^*F tensor_(O_(X x Y)) pr_Y^*G. Pullbacks and tensor products use the full structure sheaves.

proofs.title: The two completed tensor constructions and their elementary functorial properties
proofs.statement: Projective completion preserves open surjections of Frechet spaces. Injective completion preserves closed topological embeddings. Tensoring a continuous injective map with the identity by injective completion also gives an injective map, without asserting its image is closed.
proof: For continuous seminorms p on E and q on F, define pi_(p,q)(t) as the infimum of sum_i p(x_i)q(y_i) over finite expressions t=sum_i x_i tensor y_i. Define epsilon_(p,q)(t) as the supremum of |(xi tensor eta)(t)| over linear functionals satisfying |xi|<=p and |eta|<=q. These are seminorms: combine finite expressions for the projective triangle inequality, and take a supremum of absolute values for the injective one. Every eligible pair of functionals bounds every projective expression, so epsilon<=pi. Hahn-Banach supplies functionals attaining p(x) and q(y) on a specified pair of vectors after passing to their seminorm quotients. Thus both seminorms equal p(x)q(y) on x tensor y, including the zero-seminorm cases.

Use all pairs from countable defining seminorm families and complete after dividing out the common zero subspace. The resulting spaces are Hausdorff Frechet spaces; a diagonal sequence of seminorm tolerances gives a complete translation-invariant metric. If a:E->E' and b:F->F' are continuous, a target pair p',q' is bounded on their images by C p and D q for some source pair. The induced algebraic tensor map then satisfies the pi estimate with factor CD. Pulling back the functionals gives the same estimate for epsilon. Both maps consequently extend to the corresponding completions.

Suppose a and b are open surjections. Given source seminorms p,q, their quotient seminorms p'(x')=inf_(a(x)=x') p(x) and q'(y')=inf_(b(y)=y') q(y) are continuous: their open unit balls are the images of the source open balls. A finite target tensor expression with small sum_i p'(x'_i)q'(y'_i) can be lifted, term by term, with the sum of source products arbitrarily close to that target sum. Approximation of a completed target tensor by algebraic tensors now shows that the closure of the image of any source projective-seminorm neighbourhood contains a target neighbourhood. A finite intersection of source constraints can be dominated by one pair after taking maxima, so this holds for every source neighbourhood.

Here is the completion argument which turns this last property into actual openness and surjectivity. For a continuous linear map T:P->Q between Frechet spaces, suppose closure(T(V)) is a neighbourhood of zero whenever V is. Given a closed absolutely convex neighbourhood V, choose absolutely convex neighbourhoods V_n inside 2^(-n-1)V, and small enough that p_j(x)<=2^(-n) on V_n whenever j<=n, where p_j define P. Choose open W_n contained in closure(T(V_n)) and in the nth member of a shrinking neighbourhood basis of Q. Starting with y_0 in W_0, choose x_n in V_n such that y_(n+1)=y_n-T(x_n) belongs to W_(n+1); density in the indicated closure allows this choice. The series sum_n x_n converges in P, its sum lies in V, and y_n tends to zero. Hence T(sum_n x_n)=y_0. Thus W_0 is contained in T(V). This proves openness; a linear range containing a neighbourhood is all of Q. Apply this argument to the completed projective tensor map.

For a closed topological subspace K of E, a continuous seminorm on K is dominated by the restriction of a continuous seminorm on E. Hahn-Banach extends every functional controlled by a restricted ambient seminorm without increasing that bound. Consequently the injective tensor topology on K tensor F is exactly the topology inherited from E tensor_epsilon F; this can first be checked with the ambient defining seminorms and then with the dominated subspace seminorms. The induced map on completions is a topological embedding. Its image is closed because its domain is complete. The same reasoning applies in both factors.

For the weaker claim, let j:F->G be any continuous injective map and let t in E hat_epsilon F map to zero. Each xi in E' gives a continuous evaluation xi tensor Id_F:E hat_epsilon F->F. Applying j to this evaluation gives zero, so the evaluation itself is zero. It follows that every scalar evaluation xi tensor eta is zero on t. For a Cauchy sequence of algebraic tensors, its defining epsilon seminorm equals the supremum of these evaluations also in the limit: the convergence is uniform over each pair of seminorm-controlled dual balls. Thus all defining seminorms of t are zero. This proves injectivity, but makes no assertion of a topological embedding when j has nonclosed image.

The scalar-valued continuous dual of E hat_pi F is the space of jointly continuous bilinear forms on E x F. Indeed a continuous bilinear form is bounded by C p(x)q(y) for suitable continuous seminorms; its linearization is bounded by C pi_(p,q) and extends to the completion. Conversely such a bound gives a continuous bilinear form on pure tensors. These two constructions are inverse.

proofs.title: Nuclear maps, factorizations, and the binuclear subspace argument
proofs.statement: Nuclear maps form an operator ideal and factor through a Banach space. A nuclear map between Banach spaces factors through a Hilbert space. A composition of two nuclear Banach-space maps can be corestricted to a closed subspace containing its range or descended through a closed subspace of its kernel while retaining nuclearity.
proof: Consider T(x)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(x)y_j as defined above. There is a continuous seminorm p controlling all |xi_j|. For each target seminorm q, boundedness of the y_j supplies M_q=sup_j q(y_j)<infinity. The tails on p(x)<=1 are bounded by M_q sum_(j>N)|lambda_j|. They therefore converge in every target seminorm, uniformly on that neighbourhood; completeness gives a continuous linear map. Precomposing or postcomposing by continuous linear maps preserves respectively equicontinuity of the functionals or boundedness of the vectors. This proves the operator-ideal property. Concatenating two representations proves closure under finite sums.

A Banach factorization requires no injectivity statement about any tensor-to-operator map. Define alpha:E->ell^1 by alpha(x)=(lambda_j xi_j(x))_j; its norm is at most p(x) sum_j|lambda_j|. Define beta:ell^1->F by beta(c)=sum_j c_j y_j. For each q its norm estimate is q(beta(c))<=M_q ||c||_1, so the series converges in F and beta is continuous. Then T=beta alpha. For Banach spaces, use the nuclear norm inf sum_j ||a_j|| ||b_j|| over all representations T(x)=sum_j a_j(x)b_j. It is the quotient norm on representations; no uniqueness of the representing tensor is needed or asserted.

If T:E->F is nuclear between Banach spaces, choose a representation with sum_j ||a_j||||b_j|| finite. Discard zero terms and rescale each pair so that ||a_j||=||b_j||=sqrt(||a_j||||b_j||). The maps u:E->ell^2, u(x)=(a_j(x))_j, and v:ell^2->F, v(c)=sum_j c_j b_j, are bounded: both bounds follow from Cauchy-Schwarz and the summability of the squared rescaled norms. The last series converges absolutely in F for every c in ell^2. Thus T=v u factors through a Hilbert space.

For clarity, a closed subspace H_1 of a Hilbert space H has a bounded orthogonal projection. For x in H choose a sequence h_n in H_1 whose distances to x approach the infimum. The parallelogram identity shows h_n is Cauchy, since (h_n+h_m)/2 is another candidate. Its limit h realizes the infimum. Varying h along any real and imaginary scalar multiple of a vector in H_1 shows x-h is orthogonal to H_1. This decomposition is unique, linear in x, and its H_1 component has norm at most ||x||. It also identifies H/H_1 isometrically with H_1's orthogonal complement.

Now let E --f--> F --g--> G be nuclear Banach-space maps and suppose gf(E) is contained in a closed T contained in G. Factor g=v u through a Hilbert space H and put H_1=v^(-1)(T). This is closed, and u f(E) is contained in H_1. Therefore gf, with codomain T, is the composition E --f--> F --u--> H --P_(H_1)--> H_1 --v|_(H_1)--> T. All maps other than f are bounded; the last map is bounded for T's subspace norm. The ideal property proves nuclearity into T.

For descent, assume S is a closed subspace of E killed by gf. Factor f=v u through H and let H_1 be the closure of u(S). The bounded map gv kills H_1. The map x+S -> u(x)+H_1 from E/S to H/H_1 is well-defined and bounded, since one can take the infimum of ||u(x+s)|| over s in S. Identify this quotient with H_1's orthogonal complement. Composing with v restricted to that complement and then with the nuclear map g gives precisely the descended map E/S->G. Hence it is nuclear. The closure in the definition of H_1 is essential.

A nuclear map is compact in the locally convex sense that some neighbourhood has relatively compact image. Use p(x)<=1 as above. Every finite partial sum has totally bounded image, because its coefficients are bounded and its range is finite dimensional. For any finite list of target seminorms, the common tail bound tends uniformly to zero. The full image is therefore totally bounded. Its closure is compact in the complete metrizable target. Finally, tensoring two nuclear Banach-space maps gives a nuclear map for either completed tensor norm: multiply their scalar coefficients, use the product functionals, and use the tensor products of their bounded vectors. The absolute coefficient sum is the product of the two absolute sums.

proofs.title: Stability and the Banach-factor test for nuclear Frechet spaces
proofs.statement: Closed subspaces, separated quotients, countable products and countable inverse limits of nuclear Frechet spaces are nuclear; so is the completed projective tensor of two such spaces. For a nuclear domain, a continuous map is nuclear precisely when it factors continuously through a Banach space. Closed corestriction and closed-kernel descent of a nuclear map with nuclear domain are nuclear.
proof: Write E_j for the p_j completion in the definition of a nuclear space. If a:E->M is continuous and M is Banach, its norm is bounded by C p_j for some j. Extend it to a bounded map E_j->M and factor a as E->E_(j+1)->E_j->M. The middle map is nuclear. Composing further with any continuous M->F is nuclear by NS-1. Conversely every nuclear map has the ell^1 factorization of NS-1. This proves the Banach-factor test.

Let K be closed in E. For every j, its completion for the restricted seminorm p_j is the closed subspace K_j=closure(image(K->E_j)). The map K_(j+2)->K_j comes from the composition E_(j+2)->E_(j+1)->E_j restricted on its domain to K_(j+2) and corestricted on its codomain to K_j. The first restricted map and the second map are nuclear by the ideal property. The binuclear corestriction argument of NS-1 proves the required nuclearity. The even subsequence of the restricted seminorms still defines the topology of K. Completeness follows from K being closed; hence K is nuclear.

Equip E/K with the quotient seminorms bar_p_j(x+K)=inf_(k in K) p_j(x+k). They define its quotient topology, and its bar_p_j completion is Q_j=E_j/K_j. To check the last assertion, the displayed quotient norm agrees on the dense image of E/K with the distance to K_j in E_j, and the latter quotient is Banach. The composition E_(j+2)->E_(j+1)->E_j->Q_j is binuclear and kills K_(j+2), since it kills the dense image of K there. NS-1 therefore gives a nuclear map Q_(j+2)->Q_j. The quotient is Hausdorff because K is closed; the images of a countable neighbourhood basis give metrizability. To see completeness, let (z_n) be a quotient Cauchy sequence. Choose a subsequence so that its jth successive difference belongs to the image of {x:p_k(x)<2^(-j) for k<=j}; this is possible because those images are neighbourhoods. Lift each difference to a vector in that set and add the successive lifts to a lift of the initial term. The resulting representatives are Cauchy in every p_k, so converge in E. Their quotient limit is the limit of the original Cauchy sequence, since it is the limit of a subsequence. Thus the even quotient seminorm sequence proves nuclearity of E/K.

For a sequence of nuclear spaces E^(k), fix a nuclear defining family p_j^(k) on each. On their product use r_j(x)=max_(k<=j) p_j^(k)(x_k). Its Banach completion is the finite product of the corresponding E_j^(k). The transition for j+1 to j has finitely many nuclear diagonal blocks; its additional coordinate maps to zero. Finite sums and bounded coordinate maps preserve nuclearity, so the product is nuclear. An inverse limit of a countable system of such spaces is the closed subspace of the product defined by the continuous compatibility equations. The subspace case therefore gives the inverse-limit claim without assuming surjectivity of the transition maps.

For two nuclear spaces E,F, use diagonal projective tensor seminorms pi_(p_j,q_j); these are cofinal among all pairs. Their Banach completions identify with E_j hat_pi F_j. Indeed the seminorm first factors through E/ker(p_j) tensor F/ker(q_j), where it is the projective norm; passing to dense Banach completions preserves that norm, as is seen either by approximating each factor in finite expressions or by extending bounded bilinear forms and applying Hahn-Banach. The transition map is the tensor of the two nuclear transition maps, hence nuclear by NS-1. Thus E hat_pi F is nuclear.

Suppose T:E->F is nuclear, E is nuclear, and T(E) is contained in a closed subspace L of F. Factor T as E --a--> M --b--> F with M Banach. Then M_1=b^(-1)(L) is a closed Banach subspace, and a:E->M_1 and b|_(M_1):M_1->L are continuous. The Banach-factor test makes the corestricted map nuclear. If instead a closed K contained in E is killed by T, let M_0=closure(a(K)). The map b kills M_0, so the descended map factors as E/K -> M/M_0 -> F. Its domain is nuclear by the quotient result, and its middle space is Banach. Apply the same test. Neither argument licenses a corresponding assertion for a lone nuclear map with an arbitrary nonnuclear domain.

proofs.title: Exact tensors, kernels of nonclosed-image maps, and countable products
proofs.statement: If one Frechet factor is nuclear, pi and epsilon give the same completed tensor. Tensoring with a nuclear Frechet space is exact on short exact Frechet sequences, preserves the kernel of any continuous map between Frechet spaces, and commutes with countable products.
source_locators: Demailly IX.5.10-5.11 and 5.17; kernel and product details supplied here
proof: First let T:E->F be a nuclear map of Banach spaces and let G be Banach. In a nuclear representation of T, contraction of a tensor t by a functional xi produces an element (xi tensor Id_G)t with norm at most ||xi|| times ||t||_epsilon: apply every norm-one functional of G and then Hahn-Banach. Applying this estimate to all terms of T proves ||(T tensor Id_G)t||_pi <= ||T||_nuclear ||t||_epsilon after taking the infimum over representations. The series giving this map converges in F hat_pi G. Consequently it extends continuously from E hat_epsilon G to F hat_pi G.

For nuclear E, apply that estimate to E_(j+1)->E_j and to each Banach seminorm completion F_q. On E tensor F it yields pi_(p_j,q) <= C_j epsilon_(p_(j+1),q). Together with epsilon<=pi, these inequalities show that the two locally convex tensor topologies agree. Their Hausdorff completions are therefore canonically the same. Symmetry gives the assertion if F rather than E is nuclear.

Consider a short exact sequence 0->K->E --a--> Q->0. If F is nuclear, all three tensor products with F have the common topology just established. If instead E is nuclear, NS-2 makes K and Q nuclear, so the same conclusion holds for arbitrary Frechet F. NS-0 gives a closed embedding K hat_tensor F->E hat_tensor F and an open surjection E hat_tensor F->Q hat_tensor F. To identify the kernel, let a continuous scalar functional on E hat_tensor F annihilate the former image. By the projective universal property it is a continuous bilinear form B on E x F vanishing on K x F. It descends to a jointly continuous bilinear form on Q x F: if |B(x,y)|<=C p(x)q(y), take the infimum over representatives of x+K, and the quotient seminorm of p is continuous because a is open. Its linear extension factors through Q hat_tensor F and hence annihilates the kernel of a hat_tensor Id_F. Hahn-Banach separation by continuous functionals, applied to the closed image of K hat_tensor F, shows that this image equals that kernel.

For a general continuous a:E->G, its kernel K is closed, while a(E) need not be. Factor a into the open quotient E->E/K and the continuous injective map j:E/K->G. With F nuclear, short exactness proves that the kernel of the first tensor map is F hat_tensor K. The second tensor map is injective by the final injectivity assertion of NS-0, applied with the epsilon topology. Therefore ker(Id_F hat_tensor a)=F hat_tensor K. This step does not put a quotient topology on a(E), does not complete it as a replacement codomain, and does not assume its image is closed.

Let P=product_i E_i. A cofinal family of its seminorms is r(x)=max_(i in I) q_i(x_i) for finite I. For any p on F and algebraic t in F tensor P, one has epsilon_(p,r)(t)=max_(i in I) epsilon_(p,q_i)(t_i), where t_i is its ith coordinate tensor. Indeed a functional bounded by r depends only on the coordinates in I and decomposes into coordinate functionals with the sum of their dual bounds at most one, by the dual norm of a finite maximum product. This gives the inequality <=; evaluation on a single coordinate gives >=. Thus F tensor_epsilon P maps topologically into product_i(F hat_epsilon E_i). Its range is dense: approximate finitely many prescribed coordinate tensors by finite algebraic sums and insert each into the corresponding coordinate of P, zero elsewhere. Completing gives the canonical topological isomorphism F hat_epsilon P -> product_i(F hat_epsilon E_i). When F is nuclear these are the unsuffixed tensors claimed. Finite products and tensoring with a finite-dimensional free vector space are included.

The symmetry and associativity maps on algebraic projective tensors extend to completions. In the triple case both groupings have the topology defined by inf sum_i p(x_i)q(y_i)r(z_i); expanding finite expressions and taking infima gives the two inequalities needed for equality. A tensor involving a completed factor is approximated by finite algebraic expressions in that factor for every finite list of seminorms. This proves density of the common algebraic triple tensor and hence the asserted completed identification. In the nuclear cases used below the same maps apply to the common tensor topology. No cohomological Kunneth formula is being inferred when a complex has non-Hausdorff cohomology.

proofs.title: Nuclearity of section spaces without discarding nilpotents
proofs.statement: For every coherent sheaf F on a second-countable full complex space X, Gamma(X,F), with its canonical coherent-section Frechet topology, is nuclear.
source_locators: Demailly IX.5.12, with the recorded radius correction, and IX.5.18-5.19
proof: Begin with a polydisc D=product_(i=1)^N { |z_i-a_i|<R_i }. Give O(D) the seminorm p_r(h)=sup_(|z_i-a_i|<=rR_i)|h(z)| for 0<r<1. Choose 0<r<s<1. If a_alpha(h) is the Taylor coefficient at a, Cauchy's estimate gives |a_alpha(h)|<=p_s(h) product_i(sR_i)^(-alpha_i). It extends to a bounded functional on the p_s completion. The monomial m_alpha(z)=(z-a)^alpha has p_r norm product_i(rR_i)^(alpha_i). The restriction map from the p_s completion to the p_r completion consequently has nuclear expansion with lambda_alpha=(r/s)^(|alpha|), xi_alpha=product_i(sR_i)^(alpha_i) a_alpha, and y_alpha=m_alpha/product_i(rR_i)^(alpha_i). Both the functional and vector norms are at most one.

The sum of the absolute coefficients is product_(i=1)^N sum_(k>=0)(r/s)^k=(1-r/s)^(-N). The series converges uniformly on the smaller closed polydisc and agrees with restriction on O(D), hence on its p_s completion by density. For N=0 the space is C and the assertion is finite dimensional. An increasing sequence r_j tending to one defines the topology of O(D), and its transition maps go from radius r_(j+1) to radius r_j. They are nuclear by the estimate just proved. In particular the direction is larger radius to smaller radius; no holomorphic extension from a smaller disc is asserted.

Locally embed a full analytic chart A of X as a closed subspace of an ambient open subset Omega of C^N. The pushed-forward sheaf i_*F is coherent. After shrinking around a point, choose a finite presentation O_Omega^r -> O_Omega^s -> i_*F -> 0 and a polydisc D contained in that neighbourhood. The kernels and images are coherent. Cartan B on the ambient D, applied to the two short exact sequences of this presentation, gives the section sequence O(D)^r -> O(D)^s -> Gamma(A intersection D,F) -> 0. The last arrow is a continuous surjection between the already established coherent-section Frechet spaces, so it is open. Its kernel is closed. Thus Gamma(A intersection D,F) is a topological quotient of the nuclear space O(D)^s and is nuclear by NS-2.

Choose a countable cover (U_i) of X by such small charts. The sheaf gluing axiom identifies Gamma(X,F) with the compatible families in product_i Gamma(U_i,F). This is a closed subspace: compatibility is the vanishing of continuous differences of restrictions into the Hausdorff spaces Gamma(U_i intersection U_j,F). The canonical topology on sections is the topology induced by these local presentations and restriction seminorms, as in the bound coherent-section provider. Equivalently the continuous bijection to the closed compatible-family subspace is a homeomorphism by the Frechet open mapping theorem. NS-2 now proves nuclearity. At no point was a defining ideal replaced by its radical; the local modules, presentations and kernels are those of the full structure sheaf, including all nilpotent coefficients.

proofs.title: Canonical completed product-section comparison by refined-overlap gluing
proofs.statement: For coherent F on X and G on Y there is a canonical topological isomorphism Gamma(X,F) hat_tensor Gamma(Y,G) -> Gamma(X x Y,F boxtimes G), taking s tensor t to pr_X^*s times pr_Y^*t. Both spaces retain their full, possibly nonreduced, structures.
source_locators: Demailly IX.5.20; the globalization below uses refined overlap charts rather than an unproved global finite presentation on each whole intersection
proof: For polydiscs D,D' and their structure sheaves, take compact concentric subpolydiscs K,L and the corresponding supremum seminorms p,q. For t=sum_i f_i tensor g_i the injective tensor seminorm equals sup_(z,w in K x L)|sum_i f_i(z)g_i(w)|. Point evaluations give one inequality. For the other, fix a functional xi controlled by p. The function w -> sum_i xi(f_i)g_i(w) has q-seminorm at most the displayed supremum, since xi is bounded by the supremum on K; applying a functional eta controlled by q gives the other inequality. Taylor polynomials on the product approximate every holomorphic function uniformly on each smaller product polydisc, and each polynomial is a finite sum of separated monomials. Completion, followed by NS-3, therefore identifies O(D) hat_tensor O(D') with O(D x D').

Next let X be closed in a polydisc D and suppose i_*F has a finite presentation O_D^r -> O_D^s -> i_*F -> 0 there. Let Y=D' and G=O_D'. Taking its external product with O_D' is right exact; equivalently its cokernel is computed by pulling the matrix to D x D'. The modules and image on the ambient product are coherent. Cartan B gives the right-exact sequence on global sections O(D x D')^r -> O(D x D')^s -> Gamma(X x D',F boxtimes O_D') -> 0. On the other hand the section presentation on D has closed image at O(D)^s and is a quotient presentation of Gamma(X,F). NS-3, factoring that presentation through its closed image, yields the right-exact sequence O(D)^r hat_tensor O(D') -> O(D)^s hat_tensor O(D') -> Gamma(X,F) hat_tensor O(D') -> 0. The free-space identifications in the preceding paragraph intertwine the matrices, hence induce the desired isomorphism on the two cokernels. All spaces are Frechet, so the continuous bijection is a homeomorphism.

If also Y is closed in a polydisc D' and j_*G has a finite presentation there, external product of that presentation with i_*F gives a right-exact coherent sequence on D x D'. Cartan B again gives its exact section cokernel. The corresponding sequence tensoring the section presentation of G by Gamma(X,F) is exact by NS-3 and nuclearity from NS-4. The first two vertical maps are the isomorphisms already established for F with a free structure sheaf. Their compatibility with the presentation matrix identifies the two cokernels. This proves the assertion when both pairs have such finite ambient presentations. This argument only used right exactness of pullback and tensor for the presentations; it did not silently assume either coherent sheaf is locally free.

Fix now a pair (X,F) of that local presented kind, but allow Y,G to be arbitrary. Cover Y by countably many small charts U_i on which G has a finite ambient presentation. For each pair i,j cover U_i intersection U_j by countably many further small presented charts V_(ij,k). Such covers exist by coherence and second countability. Put P=product_i Gamma(U_i,G) and Q=product_(i,j,k) Gamma(V_(ij,k),G). Define delta:P->Q by restricting the difference of the ith and jth entries. The sheaf gluing axiom says Gamma(Y,G)=ker(delta). This description needs neither a finite presentation on the whole overlap nor any closed-image property of delta.

Let A=Gamma(X,F), which is nuclear by NS-4. NS-3 identifies A hat_tensor Gamma(Y,G) with the kernel of A hat_tensor P -> A hat_tensor Q and identifies those tensor products with the products of the individual tensor factors. For every U_i and every V_(ij,k), the already proved local comparison turns those factors into the corresponding section spaces on X x U_i or X x V_(ij,k). The isomorphisms commute with restrictions because on pure tensors they are the actual pullback-product maps, and pure tensors are dense. The resulting kernel is exactly Gamma(X x Y,F boxtimes G), by gluing on the cover (X x U_i), tested on its refined overlaps (X x V_(ij,k)). This is a topological identification of closed kernels in products of Frechet spaces. Notice that no tensor/cohomology interchange or Hausdorffness of any positive-degree cohomology was used.

Finally take arbitrary X,F as well. Cover X by presented charts and their pairwise overlaps by further presented charts exactly as above. For each of these charts the comparison with the arbitrary fixed (Y,G) was just proved. Repeat the kernel-and-product argument, now tensoring by the nuclear space Gamma(Y,G). It gives the desired comparison globally. Every stage agrees on pure sections with s tensor t -> pr_X^*s times pr_Y^*t, which makes the global map canonical and compatible with restrictions in either variable and with morphisms of coherent sheaves. All local presentations and external products used full analytic modules, so the assertion includes nonreduced X and Y.

proofs.title: Nuclear coherent restriction and its explicit free relative form
proofs.statement: If V is relatively compact in U and F is coherent on U, restriction Gamma(U,F)->Gamma(V,F) is nuclear. Its valid closed corestrictions and closed-kernel descents are nuclear. For a nuclear unital Frechet algebra A and a nuclear map r:V_0->W_0 of nuclear Frechet spaces, Id_A hat_tensor r is A-nuclear between the free modules A hat_tensor V_0 and A hat_tensor W_0 in the explicit sense stated below.
source_locators: Demailly IX.5.13, 5.16, 5.36 and the free part of 5.37
proof: First note why a compact map T:E->F of Frechet spaces factors through a Banach space. Choose a continuous seminorm p whose open unit ball lies in a neighbourhood with relatively compact image. For every target seminorm q there is C_q such that q(Tx)<=C_q on p(x)<1. Scaling gives q(Tx)<=C_q p(x) for every x, and if p(x)=0 the same conclusion follows by scaling x arbitrarily. Thus T vanishes on ker(p), is uniformly continuous from the normed quotient E/ker(p) for each q, and extends uniquely to a continuous map E_p->F, since F is complete. This provides the Banach factorization E->E_p->F.

Use the compact restriction result of the pinned coherent-section provider with its maps explicitly oriented as follows. On nested standard charts A intersection D' inside A intersection D, with D' relatively compact in D and a fixed finite ambient presentation, Montel compactness gives a compact free restriction O(D)^s->O(D')^s. Composing with the target section quotient remains compact. The source quotient O(D)^s->Gamma(A intersection D,F) is open: the image of a neighbourhood on which the free map is relatively compact is a neighbourhood in the source section space. The induced coherent restriction is therefore compact. For general V relatively compact in U, cover closure(V) by finitely many smaller such charts U'_i with larger charts U_i contained in U. Map Gamma(U,F) to the finite product of Gamma(U_i,F), then restrict compactly to the product of Gamma(U'_i,F), then continuously to the product of Gamma(V intersection U'_i,F). This composite is compact. The section space Gamma(V,F) embeds as the closed subspace of compatible families in that last product. The composite takes values there; its relatively compact closure remains there because that subspace is closed. It follows that Gamma(U,F)->Gamma(V,F) itself is compact. This uses the embedding into the product, not a supposed map from an arbitrary family back to a glued section.

Both section spaces are Frechet and the domain is nuclear by NS-4. The Banach factorization proved above and NS-2 now make restriction nuclear. If its range lies in a specified closed subspace of the target, or it kills a specified closed subspace of its domain, the corresponding map is nuclear by the last part of NS-2. These conclusions apply only with those stated closedness conditions; no arbitrary quotient or nonclosed submodule is substituted.

For the relative assertion, assume multiplication in A is jointly continuous and use the free A-module action on A hat_tensor V_0 through its first factor. Say an A-linear map T:M->N is A-nuclear if it has an expansion T(x)=sum_j lambda_j phi_j(x)n_j, where sum_j|lambda_j| is finite, phi_j:M->A are continuous A-linear maps forming an equicontinuous family, and n_j form a bounded sequence in N. Equicontinuity here means that for each continuous seminorm p on A there is a continuous seminorm s on M such that p(phi_j(x))<=s(x) for every j,x. This is not the scalar nuclear-map definition.

Write r(v)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(v)w_j with equicontinuous scalar xi_j and bounded w_j. Set phi_j=Id_A hat_tensor xi_j:A hat_tensor V_0->A and n_j=1_A tensor w_j in A hat_tensor W_0. These maps are A-linear. Choose a continuous q on V_0 with |xi_j(v)|<=q(v) for all j. For every seminorm p on A, the projective tensor estimate gives p(phi_j(x))<=pi_(p,q)(x), proving the stated equicontinuity. The n_j are bounded because each tensor seminorm is bounded by p(1_A) times the corresponding bounded seminorm of w_j. The series sum_j lambda_j phi_j(x)n_j converges in A hat_tensor W_0 and defines a continuous map: on elementary expressions its target (p,q')-seminorm is bounded by pi_(p,q)(x) times sup_j q'(w_j) sum_j|lambda_j|, and the same bound passes to the completion. On pure tensors the series is Id_A tensor r, so by density it is its completed extension. This proves A-nuclearity.

In particular take A=O(S) for a full complex space S. Its multiplication is jointly continuous, as follows locally from the multiplication of holomorphic representatives and then from the quotient presentations; its scalar section space is nuclear by NS-4. NS-5 identifies A hat_tensor O(U) with O(S x U). A relatively compact vertical restriction U->V therefore gives an A-nuclear map O(S x U)->O(S x V), and the same holds for finite free sums. This is the free vertical input for the relative construction. It is not a proof of A-subnuclear corestriction for general coherent modules, of transverse analytic base restriction, or of the finite-complex theorem. For infinite-dimensional A an A-nuclear map of this form need not be a scalar compact map; no such implication has been used.

chapters.title: Balanced nuclear tensors and analytic restriction

conventions.label: algebras
conventions.text: A and the other base algebras are commutative unital nuclear Frechet algebras over C. Their multiplication, and all module actions, are jointly continuous. All modules in this packet are nuclear Hausdorff Frechet spaces before a balanced quotient is formed.

conventions.label: plain_tensor
conventions.text: The completed scalar tensor is the common projective/injective tensor of NS-3. A nuclear free A-module is A hat_tensor V for a nuclear Frechet space V, with A acting in the first factor; it need not have finite rank.

conventions.label: balanced_quotient
conventions.text: E hat_tensor_A F denotes (E hat_tensor F)/im(delta), where delta:E hat_tensor A hat_tensor F -> E hat_tensor F sends x tensor a tensor y to ax tensor y minus x tensor ay. The image is not silently replaced by its closure. This quotient, with its quotient topology, can be non-Hausdorff; no further Hausdorff completion is taken.

conventions.label: homology
conventions.text: Chain differentials lower the index. Homology is ker(d_q)/im(d_(q+1)), with the quotient topology, which need not be Hausdorff. The long exact sequences and the positive-degree resolution comparison below assert algebraic exactness/isomorphisms, not unproved topological strictness.

conventions.label: transverse
conventions.text: E and F are transverse over A if their balanced tensor is Hausdorff and all positive-degree bar-derived Tor groups vanish. In that case their degree-zero balanced tensor is a nuclear Frechet space.

conventions.label: bounded_right
conventions.text: For cochain complexes, bounded on the right means E^q=0 for q>N for some finite N. No lower bound is implied.

conventions.label: analytic_scope
conventions.text: BT-3 is formulated on ambient Stein manifolds, with arbitrary coherent modules, exactly as used in the graph-chart construction of the retained S6 theorem. It does not require the original total space or its fibres to be smooth or reduced. The statement is about open subsets of the base, not points or arbitrary analytic base changes.

proofs.title: The balanced quotient and a split underlying-vector-space bar resolution
proofs.statement: Every nuclear A-module has a nuclear free augmented bar resolution split as a complex of topological C-vector spaces. Balancing a nuclear free module against any nuclear module gives the ordinary completed scalar tensor of its generator space with that module, as a topological isomorphism.
proof: For a nuclear A-module F set L_q=A^(hat_tensor(q+1)) hat_tensor F for q>=0 and L_(-1)=F. Let A act on the first A-factor. The augmentation is d_0(a_0 tensor y)=a_0 y. For q>=1, d_q is the sum of the q adjacent-product maps, indexed i=0,...,q-1 with coefficient (-1)^i, and the final action map with coefficient (-1)^q: the latter sends a_0 tensor ... tensor a_q tensor y to a_0 tensor ... tensor a_(q-1) tensor a_q y. Joint continuity of multiplication and action, followed by the projective tensor universal property, defines each of these maps on the completed tensors. Each map is A-linear; the spaces L_q are nuclear free by NS-2.

Write face_i for the unsigned adjacent-product or final-action map. Associativity of multiplication and of the module action gives face_i face_j=face_(j-1) face_i whenever i<j, with source in the appropriate bar degree. The terms of d_(q-1)d_q pair off using this identity and have opposite signs. Thus d squared is zero, including the augmentation equation. These identities hold first on pure tensors and then on the completions by continuity and density.

Define h_q:L_q->L_(q+1) by inserting 1_A at the front, also for q=-1. In d_(q+1)h_q the first face removes the inserted unit and gives the identity. Every other face is minus the matching term of h_(q-1)d_q. Hence d_(q+1)h_q+h_(q-1)d_q=Id_(L_q), with d_0 h_(-1)=Id_F at the augmented degree. These are continuous C-linear maps; h is not asserted to be A-linear. For q>=0, the image of d_(q+1) equals ker(d_q), which is closed. The map d_(q+1)h_q is a continuous projection onto that kernel. The augmentation is likewise split by h_(-1). This proves both exactness and the claimed underlying topological splitting.

Now let P=A hat_tensor V. On P hat_tensor F define Q((a tensor v) tensor y)=v tensor ay and S(v tensor y)=(1 tensor v) tensor y. Both maps are continuous and QS=Id. Define H:P hat_tensor F -> P hat_tensor A hat_tensor F by H((a tensor v) tensor y)=(1 tensor v) tensor a tensor y. If delta is the balancing map, then delta H=Id-SQ; also Q delta=0. These identities extend from pure tensors to the completions. Consequently ker(Q)=im(delta), not merely its closure. This image is closed because Q has Hausdorff target. The quotient P hat_tensor_A F is canonically V hat_tensor F, with a continuous inverse induced by S. Symmetry gives E hat_tensor_A (A hat_tensor V)=E hat_tensor V. In particular these free balanced products are Hausdorff and nuclear.

proofs.title: Bar-derived Tor, signed symmetry and the long exact sequence
proofs.statement: The bar complex defines balanced Tor with degree zero equal to the actual balanced quotient. It is symmetric for the commutative algebra A, has zero positive groups when either module is nuclear free, and gives the long exact Tor sequence for a short exact sequence of nuclear Frechet modules.
proof: Using BT-0 on E hat_tensor_A L_q(F), identify its qth term with T_q(E,F)=E hat_tensor A^(hat_tensor q) hat_tensor F. For q>=1 its differential on x tensor a_1 tensor ... tensor a_q tensor y is a_1 x tensor a_2 tensor ... tensor a_q tensor y, plus the adjacent interior products a_i a_(i+1) with coefficient (-1)^i for 1<=i<q, plus x tensor a_1 tensor ... tensor a_(q-1) tensor a_q y with coefficient (-1)^q. This formula follows by absorbing the first free A-factor into E. It also follows directly from BT-0 that the differential squares to zero. Define Torhat_q^A(E,F)=H_q(T(E,F)); since the degree-one differential is precisely delta, Torhat_0 is the balanced quotient as defined, without closing its relations.

The symmetry is an actual signed chain map, not an unspecified equality up to sign. In degree q put R_q(x tensor a_1 tensor ... tensor a_q tensor y)=(-1)^(q(q+1)/2) y tensor a_q tensor ... tensor a_1 tensor x. For the unsigned reversal, the face indexed i becomes the face indexed q-i, so its differential gains the factor (-1)^q. The prefactors satisfy (-1)^(q(q+1)/2) (-1)^q=(-1)^((q-1)q/2). Therefore d R_q=R_(q-1) d. Each R_q is a topological isomorphism and its inverse is the same signed reversal in the other direction. It induces symmetry of Tor, including the quotient topology in degree zero.

If E=A hat_tensor V, its balanced tensor with the augmented bar resolution of F is V hat_tensor L(F). The contraction Id_V hat_tensor h from BT-0 is well-defined as a C-linear contraction after this free identification. Thus positive homology vanishes and degree zero is V hat_tensor F. If F is nuclear free, apply the just-proved symmetry. In particular nuclear free modules are transverse to every nuclear module.

Let 0->E_1 --i--> E_2 --p--> E_3->0 be a short exact sequence of nuclear Frechet A-modules. For fixed F every bar degree is a scalar tensor with the nuclear space A^(hat_tensor q) hat_tensor F. NS-3 gives a short exact sequence of the three bar complexes in each degree, with a closed inclusion and an open surjection. The usual connecting map can be constructed explicitly: lift a cycle c in the E_3 complex to b in the E_2 term; then db=i(a) for a unique a in the E_1 term. Injectivity of i and d squared zero show da=0. Set the connecting class to [a]. Replacing b by b+i(a') changes a by da'; replacing c by c+dc' and lifting c' changes b by a boundary and does not change its connecting class.

The element chase proves exactness at all three types of positions. If the image of a cycle b from the middle complex is a boundary dc', lift c' and subtract that lifted boundary from b; the result is the image of a cycle of the first complex. If a cycle c has connecting class zero, db=i(da') for a lift b, so b-i(a') is a cycle lifting c. If a cycle a in the first complex becomes a boundary db=i(a), then p(b) is a cycle and its connecting class is [a]. Degree-zero surjectivity follows from degree-zero surjectivity of p. These statements give the whole algebraic long exact sequence, ending with E_1 hat_tensor_A F -> E_2 hat_tensor_A F -> E_3 hat_tensor_A F -> 0. Symmetry supplies the analogous sequence in the other variable.

In particular the balanced tensor functor is right exact in this algebraic sense. The last map of a balanced right-exact sequence is also open for the quotient topologies: the corresponding map of unbalanced completed scalar tensors is open by NS-3, the two balancing quotient maps are open, and the image of an open saturated set can be computed through these maps. Thus a balanced cokernel may be calculated with its actual quotient topology. None of this asserts that arbitrary higher Tor groups are Hausdorff, or that the complete long exact sequence is topologically strict.

proofs.title: Computing Tor with a nuclear free resolution without assuming an A-linear splitting
proofs.statement: If L_*->F is any exact resolution by nuclear free A-modules and continuous A-linear maps, then H_q(E hat_tensor_A L_*) is canonically Torhat_q^A(E,F). In degree zero the comparison respects the quotient topologies. The positive-degree assertion required here is algebraic.
proof: Let B_(-1)=F and B_j=ker(L_j->L_(j-1)) for j>=0, interpreting the degree-zero map as the augmentation. Exactness says B_j=im(L_(j+1)->L_j). Since it is a kernel of a continuous map to a Hausdorff space, B_j is closed and nuclear by NS-2. The induced maps L_j->B_(j-1) are surjective maps of Frechet spaces and therefore open. We have short exact sequences 0->B_j->L_j->B_(j-1)->0 in the precise category used by BT-1. No complementary A-submodule or continuous A-linear section has been assumed.

Because L_j is nuclear free, its positive Tor with E vanishes. The long exact sequence gives Torhat_m(E,B_(j-1))=Torhat_(m-1)(E,B_j) canonically for m>1, and Torhat_1(E,B_(j-1)) identifies with ker(E hat_tensor_A B_j -> E hat_tensor_A L_j). Iterating the first equality shows for q>=1 that Torhat_q(E,F) identifies with ker(E hat_tensor_A B_(q-1) -> E hat_tensor_A L_(q-1)); for q=1 this is just the second assertion with j=0.

To compare with the proposed complex, factor its differential in degree q as r_q:E hat_tensor_A L_q -> E hat_tensor_A B_(q-1), followed by j_(q-1):E hat_tensor_A B_(q-1) -> E hat_tensor_A L_(q-1). Right exactness makes r_q surjective and says ker(r_q) is the image of E hat_tensor_A B_q. That image is also im(d_(q+1)), because L_(q+1)->B_q is surjective and stays surjective after balanced tensor. It follows directly that ker(d_q)/im(d_(q+1)) maps bijectively by r_q onto ker(j_(q-1)). This is exactly the group found by dimension shifting. In degree zero, right exactness identifies the cokernel of d_1 with E hat_tensor_A F, and the open-quotient observation of BT-1 makes that identification topological.

The identifications are canonical for the given augmentation: their connecting maps were defined from lifts with an independence proof in BT-1, and r_q is induced by the actual differential. If a chain map between two such resolutions respects their augmentations, applying the same lifts to that map shows that it commutes with all these identifications. No general lifting property for nuclear free modules, which would require additional hypotheses, was used. When the resulting positive Tor groups vanish and degree zero is Hausdorff, this comparison does give a strict augmented resolution: all differential images are then kernels in Frechet terms and the augmentation target is Frechet.

proofs.title: Transverse restriction to a Stein open subset of the base
proofs.statement: Let X,Y be Stein manifolds, U contained relatively compactly in X and V contained relatively compactly in Y be Stein open sets, and U' be any Stein open subset of U. If F is coherent on X x Y, then B=O(U') and M=Gamma(U x V,F) are transverse over A=O(U), and the canonical map B hat_tensor_A M -> Gamma(U' x V,F) is a topological isomorphism. Coherent modules supported on full nonreduced analytic subspaces are included.
source_locators: Demailly IX.5.33, in the ambient manifold form used by the proof on pp. 447-448
proof: Put W=X x Y and K=closure(U) x closure(V), a compact subset of W. The pinned Stein product proposition makes W Stein. Construct a resolution on the fixed U x V as follows. Cartan A supplies global sections of F whose germs generate at every point. At any one point finitely many suffice; the coherent cokernel of their generating map has zero stalk there and therefore vanishes on a neighbourhood. A finite subcover of K consequently selects finitely many global sections giving a map u_0:O_W^(r_0)->F which is surjective near K. Its kernel F_0 on the entire W is coherent. Apply the same argument to F_0, obtaining u_1:O_W^(r_1)->F_0 surjective near K. Repeat with F_j=ker(u_j) on W. Compose u_j with the inclusion F_(j-1)->O_W^(r_(j-1)) to obtain d_j for j>=1.

These maps form a complex globally, and its augmentation and every differential are exact on U x V because every chosen map is surjective at every point of K. Although the neighbourhood of K on which a particular map is surjective can vary with j, the fixed set U x V is contained in each such neighbourhood. Thus no infinite intersection of shrinking neighbourhoods is needed. Every free term has finite rank, but the sequence may continue indefinitely to the left; no bounded finite resolution or uniform length has been claimed.

Restrict this sheaf resolution to U x V. Its kernels are coherent, and this product is Stein. Cartan B applied separately to 0->F_j->O^(r_j)->F_(j-1)->0 on that open set gives an exact sequence of global sections in every degree, including the augmentation. The section spaces are nuclear Frechet by NS-4, and the maps to their closed cycle spaces are open. Moreover NS-5 gives O(U x V)^(r_j)=A hat_tensor O(V)^(r_j), so the resolution is nuclear free over A. The same statements hold after restriction to U' x V, since U' is Stein; relative compactness of U' in U is not required.

Apply B hat_tensor_A to the section complex. BT-0 identifies each resulting term with B hat_tensor O(V)^(r_j), and NS-5 identifies that space with O(U' x V)^(r_j). These identifications send b tensor s to the product of b with the restricted section. They commute with the differentials: for a separated holomorphic coefficient this follows from multiplication and restriction, and general coefficients follow by the dense product-section identification and continuity of multiplication. Thus the tensor complex is exactly the restricted section resolution, with its actual matrices, not merely a complex having isomorphic terms.

That restricted resolution has zero positive homology and degree-zero cokernel Gamma(U' x V,F). BT-2 therefore gives vanishing of all positive Torhat groups and the claimed degree-zero identification. It is topological because both sides are the same quotient of the degree-zero free section space by the image of its preceding differential. The image is closed, being the kernel of the surjective map to the Frechet section space Gamma(U' x V,F). Thus the balanced tensor is Hausdorff, proving transversality.

The ambient hypotheses do not impose smoothness on a space supporting F. In the proper-map construction a local full analytic space is embedded, together with its map to a base chart, as a closed analytic graph in a product of Stein manifolds. Its coherent sheaf pushes forward to a coherent module on that ambient product. All equations, nilpotents and module relations stay in that module, so BT-3 applies to it without replacing the graph by its reduced space. The finite-intersection graph construction is supplied by the pinned Stein-piece lemma. This explains why the lemma covers the chartwise construction needed for the original S6 scope. It does not prove the entire finite-complex construction or extend this open-restriction statement to a point of the base.

proofs.title: Transversality through kernels, successive base algebras and bounded-right acyclic complexes
proofs.statement: Transversality is preserved in the kernel of a short exact sequence whose middle and last terms are transverse. It composes under transverse scalar extension. Tensoring a bounded-right cochain complex of transverse modules preserves acyclicity in any specified upper range.
proof: Let 0->E_1->E_2->E_3->0 be a short exact sequence and suppose E_2,E_3 are transverse to M. Their higher Tor groups vanish, so the long exact sequence makes all positive Tor groups of E_1 vanish and gives an algebraically exact sequence 0->M hat_tensor_A E_1->M hat_tensor_A E_2->M hat_tensor_A E_3->0. The first map is a continuous injection into a Hausdorff space. This forces its domain to be Hausdorff: distinct domain points have distinct images, which have disjoint open neighbourhoods whose preimages separate the points. Hence the balancing relation space defining M hat_tensor_A E_1 is closed. This domain is now nuclear Frechet by NS-2. Its image is the closed kernel of the last map; the open mapping theorem applied to its continuous bijection onto that kernel proves that it has exactly the subspace topology. The last map is open as well. This proves transversality of E_1 and strictness of the resulting short exact sequence, without assuming Hausdorffness at the start.

Let A->A_1->A_2 be continuous unital algebra maps, and suppose both A_1 and A_2 are transverse to the A-module E. Use the bar resolution L_q=A hat_tensor V_q of E. By BT-2 and transversality, A_1 hat_tensor_A L_* is an exact augmented nuclear free A_1-resolution of E_1=A_1 hat_tensor_A E, with terms A_1 hat_tensor V_q. Apply BT-2 once more over A_1. In every degree, balancing its free terms with A_2 gives A_2 hat_tensor V_q, exactly the complex obtained by balancing the original L_* with A_2 over A. The identifications commute with the differential because they are the maps induced by multiplication in A_2. Thus Torhat_q^(A_1)(A_2,E_1) is Torhat_q^A(A_2,E) for q>=0. In degree zero this is an identification of quotient topologies, by BT-2, so it is Hausdorff; in positive degrees it is zero. Therefore A_2 is transverse to E_1 over A_1. This argument uses free-term identifications, not an unproved associativity rule for arbitrary non-Hausdorff balanced quotients.

Now let E^* be a cochain complex with E^q=0 for q>N, and suppose each E^q is transverse to M. Suppose also H^q(E)=0 for q>=k. Its cycle spaces Z^q=ker(d^q) are closed nuclear submodules. For q>=k-1, the sequence 0->Z^q->E^q->Z^(q+1)->0 is exact because H^(q+1)(E)=0. Start above N with the zero cycle space. Descending one degree at a time, apply the first paragraph to this sequence; it shows Z^q is transverse to M for all q>=k-1 and that each tensored sequence is strict exact. Each individual degree is reached in finitely many steps from N; there is no assertion about an inverse limit of this induction.

For q>=k, factor the tensored differential through M hat_tensor_A Z^(q+1). The second map into M hat_tensor_A E^(q+1) is injective by the just-proved exact sequence in degree q+1. Its kernel at degree q is therefore precisely M hat_tensor_A Z^q, embedded by the sequence in degree q. The differential from degree q-1 surjects onto that same subspace by the sequence in degree q-1. Hence the tensored complex has zero cohomology in every degree q>=k, as claimed. The bound above is essential to this argument and has not been omitted.

proofs.title: The correctly signed comparison cone and preservation of a quasi-isomorphism range
proofs.statement: For bounded-right complexes E,F with all terms transverse to M, tensoring an A-linear chain map preserves the property of being an isomorphism on cohomology in degrees q>=k and a surjection in degree k-1.
source_locators: Demailly IX.5.34(d)-5.35 with the already recorded shift-sign correction
proof: For f:E^*->F^* define C^q=E^q direct_sum F^(q-1) and D^q(e,y)=(d_E e, f(e)-d_F y). The second component of D^(q+1)D^q is f(d_E e)-d_F(f(e))+d_F squared(y), which is zero because f is a cochain map. The first component is zero as well. Let F[-1]^q=F^(q-1) with differential -d_F. Then y->(0,y) and (e,y)->e give a short exact sequence of complexes 0->F[-1]->C->E->0. The connecting map H^q(E)->H^q(F) is H^q(f): a closed e lifts to (e,0), and its differential is (0,f(e)). This specifies both the shift and its differential rather than writing an unspecified equivalence up to sign.

The associated exact sequence has segment H^(q-1)(E) --H^(q-1)(f)--> H^(q-1)(F) -> H^q(C) -> H^q(E) --H^q(f)--> H^q(F). The connecting-map construction and the three element chases are exactly those given in BT-1, with degrees reindexed. This segment shows H^q(C)=0 if and only if H^(q-1)(f) is surjective and H^q(f) is injective. Therefore the stated isomorphism/surjection range for f is equivalent to acyclicity of C in degrees q>=k.

A finite direct sum of modules transverse to M is transverse: its two-sided bar complex is the finite direct sum of their bar complexes, and its degree-zero quotient is the corresponding finite direct sum of Hausdorff balanced quotients. Thus every term of C is transverse to M. The cone is bounded on the right because E and F are. BT-4 shows that M hat_tensor_A C is acyclic in degrees q>=k. The same finite direct-sum and differential formulas identify it with the cone of Id_M hat_tensor_A f. Applying the preceding exact-sequence criterion gives injectivity of the tensor map on H^q for q>=k and surjectivity for q>=k-1; combining them gives the required isomorphisms. The known incorrect matrix with second row (-f,+d_F) is not used, and no new source correction is being claimed here.

proofs.title: Coherent vertical restriction is subnuclear over the base algebra
proofs.statement: In the ambient Stein setting, let S be relatively compact and Stein in a Stein manifold Y, let U' be relatively compact in U and U relatively compact in a Stein manifold Z, with U,U' Stein. For coherent F on Y x Z, restriction Gamma(S x U,F)->Gamma(S x U',F) is O(S)-subnuclear. The nuclear and subnuclear classes have the composition properties needed in the relative construction.
proof: Use the A-nuclear definition and free restriction formula of NS-6. Call a continuous A-linear map f:E->F A-subnuclear if there is a nuclear Frechet A-module P and an open surjection p:P->E such that fp is A-nuclear. For an A-nuclear representation, precomposition by a continuous A-linear map preserves equicontinuity of the coefficient maps, and postcomposition preserves boundedness of the target vectors. The represented series is therefore A-nuclear after either composition. Concatenation of finitely many representations proves closure under finite sums.

For precomposition of a subnuclear map f with u:T->E, use the pullback P'={(t,z) in T x P:u(t)=p(z)}. It is closed in a product of nuclear Frechet modules, hence nuclear by NS-2. Its projection pi:P'->T is surjective.
