It is also open: the image of a basic product neighbourhood, intersected with P', is O_T intersection u^(-1)(p(O_P)), which is open because p is open; translations give the assertion at every point. The map (fu)pi equals (fp) followed by projection P'->P on the input, so is A-nuclear. This proves subnuclearity of fu. Postcomposition keeps the same surjection p and follows from the nuclear case. Finite sums follow by taking the fibre product of finitely many witnessing surjections over the same domain; the same closedness and openness argument applies. No automatic corestriction to an arbitrary closed target submodule is asserted.

For the analytic restriction, Cartan A on the Stein product Y x Z and compactness of closure(S) x closure(U) select finitely many global sections of F generating near that compact set, exactly as in BT-3. They give a finite free sheaf L_0 and a surjection L_0->F on S x U. Its coherent kernel has zero positive cohomology there by Cartan B. Thus p:Gamma(S x U,L_0)->Gamma(S x U,F) is a continuous open surjection of nuclear Frechet A-modules, A=O(S). Its source is A hat_tensor O(U)^r by NS-5.

In the commutative restriction square, the free vertical arrow Gamma(S x U,L_0)->Gamma(S x U',L_0) is A-nuclear by NS-6 because U' is relatively compact in U. The bottom arrow to Gamma(S x U',F) is continuous and A-linear. Its composition with the free vertical arrow is the coherent restriction composed with p. The ideal property from the first paragraph makes that composition A-nuclear. The surjection p is therefore a witness to the claimed subnuclearity. Coherent support, nilpotents and singularities remain in F; they are not removed by the free presentation.

This finishes the coherent restriction input but not the next corestriction theorem: an A-subnuclear map whose range lies in a closed submodule is not here declared subnuclear into that smaller codomain. The remaining source argument adds scalar-nuclear shrinking of the base algebra and transversality of the target quotient. Those hypotheses and their proof remain part of the open relative perturbation chain.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Algebras and modules are complex, unital and complete; the algebras in scalar extension are commutative and their multiplication and module actions are jointly continuous. All linear morphisms are continuous. Frechet spaces are Hausdorff unless an algebraic cokernel is explicitly being discussed.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: For scalar Frechet tensors use the completed projective tensor; with a nuclear factor it agrees with the injective tensor by NS-3. A balanced tensor is the quotient by the actual image of the balancing differential as in BT-0, not by its closure. It is only treated as a nuclear Frechet space once transversality or the free-module formula has proved it Hausdorff.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: A-nuclear means T(x)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(x)y_j with summable complex lambda_j, equicontinuous A-linear xi_j into A, and a bounded sequence y_j. For a nuclear domain, A-subnuclear means that precomposition with some open surjection from a nuclear Frechet A-module is A-nuclear. These are the definitions established in NS-6 and BT-6, not scalar compactness assertions.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: The open mapping theorem and the exact topologies of coherent sections are supplied by the pinned programme providers. Source references identify the mathematical route; the proof paragraphs here give the needed argument rather than treating a citation as proof closure.

proofs.title: Closed corestriction becomes subnuclear after a scalar-nuclear change of algebra
proofs.statement: Let A,B be nuclear Frechet algebras, rho:A->B a scalar-nuclear unital homomorphism, E,F nuclear Frechet A-modules, and F_1 a closed A-submodule of F. Suppose B is transverse over A to E, F and F/F_1. If f:E->F is A-subnuclear and f(E) is contained in F_1, then the induced map f_(1,B):B hat_tensor_A E -> B hat_tensor_A F_1 is B-subnuclear.
proof: Write F_B=B hat_tensor_A F and E_B=B hat_tensor_A E. Apply BT-4 to 0->F_1->F->F/F_1->0. The two assumed transverse modules on the right imply that F_(1,B) is nuclear Frechet and embeds as a closed submodule of F_B. This step supplies the closed topology needed below; no such conclusion about balanced F_1 was assumed beforehand.

First assume f is A-nuclear. Choose f(e)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(e)y_j and a scalar-nuclear representation rho(a)=sum_k mu_k eta_k(a)b_k. The map nu:E->F_B, nu(e)=1 tensor_A f(e), is represented by sum_(j,k) lambda_j mu_k (eta_k composed with xi_j)(e) (b_k tensor_A y_j). Indeed balancing moves xi_j(e) to the B factor, and the expansion of rho gives the displayed double sum. Its coefficients have finite absolute sum. The eta_k have a common bound by a single seminorm p of A; equicontinuity of the xi_j for p gives a single seminorm q of E bounding every eta_k xi_j. Boundedness of b_k and y_j makes their tensor products bounded for every projective seminorm and then for the quotient topology of F_B. Absolute convergence with these estimates proves that nu is scalar-nuclear and justifies both orders of summation.

For subnuclear f, let p:P->E be its witnessing open surjection with P nuclear and fp A-nuclear. The previous calculation makes nu p:P->F_B scalar-nuclear. This map kills the closed kernel of p. NS-2 therefore makes its descent P/ker(p)->F_B scalar-nuclear. Open mapping identifies P/ker(p) topologically with E, so nu itself is scalar-nuclear. This use of descent has a nuclear domain; it is not a general assertion about arbitrary nuclear operators on arbitrary Banach quotients.

The range of nu lies in the closed subspace F_(1,B) found in the first paragraph. Since E is nuclear, NS-2 gives a scalar-nuclear corestriction nu_1:E->F_(1,B). The map q:B hat_tensor E->E_B, b tensor e |-> b tensor_A e, is an open surjection between nuclear Frechet spaces: E_B is Hausdorff by the transversality assumption. On its source, f_(1,B) q is the composite of Id_B hat_tensor nu_1:B hat_tensor E->B hat_tensor F_(1,B) and the module action B hat_tensor F_(1,B)->F_(1,B). NS-6 makes the first map B-nuclear; the composition rule makes the composite B-nuclear. Thus q witnesses B-subnuclearity of f_(1,B). There has been no assertion that f:E->F_1 was already A-subnuclear before shrinking the algebra.

proofs.title: The radius system of a fully nuclear algebra
proofs.statement: Let A carry an increasing defining family p_r, 0<r<1, of submultiplicative seminorms. Write B_r for the Banach completion for p_r and assume B_v->B_u is scalar-nuclear whenever u<v. Let A_t be the Hausdorff completion of A for the seminorms p_r with r<t, and set A_1=A. Then A_t is fully nuclear, (A_t)_s=A_(st), and A_t'->A_t is scalar-nuclear for 0<t<t'<=1. If E is fully A-transverse, E_t=A_t hat_tensor_A E is fully A_t-transverse.
proof: Choose a countable increasing sequence of radii cofinal below t. Those seminorms define the same topology as all p_r with r<t, so the indicated separated completion is Frechet. Submultiplicativity extends multiplication to it. For a fixed r<t, the seminorm p_r extends to A_t and its Banach completion is B_r: the image of A is dense in both. Consequently the family q_s=p_(st), 0<s<1, on A_t has the same nuclear Banach transition maps as the original family. It makes A_t fully nuclear and, in particular, a nuclear Frechet space. The same argument with t=1 establishes nuclearity of A itself.

Completing A_t for q_r with r<s amounts to completing the dense image of A for p_u with u<st. Completion of that same separated seminormed system gives (A_t)_s=A_(st), with the canonical map induced by A. This identifies the maps, not merely isomorphic vector spaces.

For t<t', select radii u,v with t<=u<v<t'. There are continuous maps A_t'->B_v->B_u->A_t. The first uses the seminorm p_v. The last exists because p_r<=p_u for each r<t and A_t is complete. Their composite agrees on the dense image of A with its natural restriction map. The middle map is nuclear by assumption, hence the composite is scalar-nuclear by the ideal property NS-1. For t'=1 the same argument works directly from A. The direction is always from a larger radius to a smaller radius.

If E is fully transverse, every E_t is a Hausdorff quotient of the nuclear scalar tensor A_t hat_tensor E, and hence is nuclear Frechet. Given 0<s<1, both A_t and A_(st) are transverse to E over A. Apply the successive-base argument BT-4 to A->A_t->A_(st); it identifies A_(st) hat_tensor_(A_t) E_t with E_(st) and kills its positive Tor. Using (A_t)_s=A_(st), this is precisely full A_t-transversality of E_t. No flatness statement for the Banach stages B_t is needed.

proofs.title: Analytic radius algebras and full coherent modules
proofs.statement: For a polydisc D compactly contained in a larger polydisc D_0 and a closed full analytic subspace X of D_0, A=O(X intersection D) is fully nuclear for the quotient sup seminorms, and A_t=O(X intersection tD). If Y is a Stein manifold, V is a relatively compact Stein open in Y, and G is coherent on X x Y, then Gamma((X intersection D) x V,G) is fully A-transverse. These examples include the ambient-chart modules in the retained S6 construction and do not remove nilpotents from X or from the support of G.
proof: Start with H=O(D), p_r(h)=sup_(closure(rD))|h|, where rD has the same centre as D and all its radii multiplied by r. The p_r are submultiplicative and define compact convergence. Taylor expansion at that centre gives nuclear maps between their Banach completions for u<v: the coefficient bound on vD and monomial norm on uD produce the summable multi-index weights (u/v)^|alpha|, exactly as proved in NS-4. Taylor polynomials show O(D) is dense in O(tD) for compact convergence, so H_t=O(tD).

Let J be the full coherent ideal defining X in D_0. Cartan B on D gives A=H/J(D) as a topological quotient; the coherent section topology makes J(D) closed. Use quotient seminorms bar_p_r(h+J)=inf_(j in J(D)) p_r(h+j). They are submultiplicative: multiply arbitrary representatives of two classes, apply submultiplicativity of p_r, and take the two infima independently. The Banach stage of A for bar_p_r is H_r/J_r, where H_r is the p_r completion of H and J_r is the closure of the image of J(D) in H_r. The quotient norm formula and density verify this identification, as in NS-2.

For u<v choose w strictly between them. The maps H_v->H_w and H_w->H_u->H_u/J_u are nuclear Banach maps. Their composite kills J_v, because it kills the dense image of J(D) there. The binuclear descent of NS-1 gives a nuclear map H_v/J_v->H_u/J_u. Thus the quotient algebra A is fully nuclear. Using two nuclear transitions here is important: we have not presumed that an arbitrary single nuclear Banach operator remains nuclear after arbitrary quotient descent.

To identify its radius completion, Cartan A on D_0 and compactness of closure(D) supply finitely many sections g_1,...,g_m of J generating J near closure(D). Cartan B for the coherent kernel of O^m->J gives J(D)=sum_i O(D)g_i and J(tD)=sum_i O(tD)g_i. Polynomial approximation of each coefficient on compact subsets of tD shows that the image of J(D) is dense in J(tD). The latter is closed in O(tD). Therefore, for every r<t and every h in O(D), the infimum defining bar_p_r(h+J(D)) is unchanged if J(D) is replaced by J(tD). The dense image of A in O(tD)/J(tD) has exactly these quotient seminorms. That quotient is complete and Hausdorff by NS-2, so its identification with A_t follows. The ideal used throughout is J, never its radical.

For the transversality assertion, put U=X intersection D and U_t=X intersection tD. Closed analytic embedding i:X x Y->D_0 x Y identifies sections of a coherent G with sections of coherent i_*G. Exactness of i_* is checked on stalks, which are G at points of the closed subspace and zero elsewhere. A flabby resolution remains flabby under i_* because sections on ambient opens are sections on their intersections with X x Y. Thus sheaf cohomology is also preserved by i_*. Cartan A and B on the ambient Stein products therefore give the corresponding generation and acyclicity statements for these full closed analytic pieces. Coherence here is the usual finite local module presentation over the coherent quotient by J; regarding that presentation over the ambient structure sheaf gives coherence of i_*G.

Apply Cartan A on D_0 x Y to i_*G and select finitely many global sections generating near closure(D) x closure(V). They give O_(X x Y)^r->G, surjective on U x V, with coherent kernel on X x Y. Repeat this construction for each successive kernel, using the same compact set, to obtain a resolution by finite free sheaves in each degree. It can extend indefinitely to the left; no finite length is claimed. Each generation neighbourhood contains U x V, so the construction takes no infinite intersection of shrinking opens. Cartan B makes its section complexes exact on U x V and on every U_t x V.

By NS-5 their free terms are A hat_tensor O(V)^r and A_t hat_tensor O(V)^r, respectively. They are nuclear by NS-2 and NS-4. BT-2 computes the balanced Tor of Gamma(U x V,G) from the first free section resolution; after balancing with A_t it is the second, exact resolution. Thus all positive Tor vanish and the degree-zero balanced tensor is canonically Gamma(U_t x V,G), including its quotient topology. That section space is Hausdorff nuclear Frechet. This proves full transversality. It does not assert restriction to a point or a finite relative complex; those remain separate obligations.

proofs.title: A Banach-module perturbation has an explicit finite-generator identity
proofs.statement: Let B be a Banach algebra, S a Frechet B-module and v:S->S B-nuclear. There are an integer N, continuous B-linear R:S->S, gamma:S->B^N and Y:B^N->S with I_S=(I_S-v)R+Y gamma. Consequently S/(I_S-v)S is generated algebraically by the N vectors Y(e_j). The quotient is not asserted Hausdorff, and S need not be a scalar-nuclear space.
source_locators: IX.5.43, p. 445; explicit continuous identity supplied for the scalar-extension step of 5.42(c)
proof: Choose v(x)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(x)y_j. Equicontinuity into the normed algebra B gives a continuous seminorm p on S with ||xi_j(x)||<=p(x) for all j. Let T=ell^1(B), alpha:S->T be alpha(x)=(lambda_j xi_j(x))_j, and beta:T->S be beta(c)=sum_j c_j y_j. Then ||alpha(x)||_1<=p(x)sum_j|lambda_j|. For every seminorm q on S, continuity of the B action gives a seminorm r and a constant C with q(by)<=C||b||r(y). Boundedness of y_j implies q(beta(c))<=C sup_j r(y_j)||c||_1. Completeness of S therefore makes beta a well-defined continuous B-linear map. We have v=beta alpha.

Set w=alpha beta:T->T. It is bounded. Let P_N:T->T keep the first N coordinates and set w_tail=(I_T-P_N)w. Since p(beta(c))<=C_p||c||_1, we obtain ||w_tail(c)||_1<=C_p(sum_(j>N)|lambda_j|)||c||_1. Choose N so that the coefficient on the right is less than one. The Banach operator D=I_T-w_tail is invertible with Q=D^(-1)=sum_(k>=0)w_tail^k. The series converges in operator norm by its geometric bound; multiplying its partial sums by D and passing to the limit proves both inverse identities. Every term is B-linear, so Q is B-linear as well.

Let j_N:B^N->T be inclusion into the first N coordinates and pi_N:T->B^N the projection, so P_N=j_N pi_N. Define Y=beta j_N, gamma=pi_N w Q alpha, and R=I_S+beta Q alpha. All are continuous B-linear maps with exactly the domains and codomains in the statement. Since (I_S-v)beta=beta(I_T-w) and D=I_T-w+P_Nw, direct multiplication gives (I_S-v)R=I_S-beta alpha+beta(I_T-w)Q alpha=I_S-beta P_N w Q alpha. Adding Y gamma gives I_S, as required.

For each x in S the identity expresses x as (I_S-v)R(x)+sum_(j=1)^N gamma_j(x)y_j. Passing to the algebraic quotient therefore gives a surjection B^N->S/(I_S-v)S. This is finite generation without a closed-image inference. We retain the continuous maps R,gamma,Y rather than tensoring this quotient, which may fail to be a Frechet space. In particular a scalar finite-rank conclusion was neither used nor obtained when B is infinite dimensional.

proofs.title: Free scalar extension and the reductions used by perturbation
proofs.statement: Continuous algebra homomorphisms extend maps between topologically free modules functorially. This extension preserves nuclear representations and finite-generator identities in the cases below. An A-subnuclear u:E->F, with a surjective f:E->F and fully transverse nuclear E,F, can be reduced after every transverse base change to f':P->F surjective and u'=f'v, where P=A hat_tensor M is nuclear free and v:P->P is A-nuclear.
source_locators: IX.5.42(a)-(c), pp. 445-446; continuous-map extension made explicit
proof: For a continuous unital algebra map rho:A->B and a nuclear Frechet space M, set P_A(M)=A hat_tensor M and P_B(M)=B hat_tensor M. In this paragraph B can be Banach and need not be nuclear. The projective tensor suffices. A continuous A-linear T:P_A(M)->P_A(N) is determined by t(m)=T(1 tensor m). Compose t with iota_N=rho hat_tensor Id_N into P_B(N), then use the continuous B action to extend b tensor m |-> b iota_N(t(m)) to a continuous B-linear T_B:P_B(M)->P_B(N). Joint continuity gives the needed projective tensor estimate, and the complete target gives the extension. On pure tensors T_B iota_M=iota_N T; density extends this equality to P_A(M). Applying that intertwining identity once more proves (T'U)_B=T'_B U_B whenever the composition is defined. Identity maps are preserved. This also applies to finite free modules by taking M or N to be a finite-dimensional space.

If A->B->C is a second change of algebra, the same construction over B extends every continuous B-linear map P_B(M)->P_B(N). The defining formulas on 1 tensor m show (T_B)_C=T_C. Thus any finite identity between such maps extends to C, whether or not B or C is flat over the previous algebra. No tensor functor on a non-Hausdorff quotient is involved.

Suppose v:P_A(M)->P_A(M) has an A-nuclear representation. For each coefficient xi_j, its B-valued extension is determined by m |-> rho(xi_j(1 tensor m)). Given a seminorm b on B, continuity of rho bounds b(rho(a)) by a seminorm a_0 on A. Equicontinuity of the xi_j bounds a_0(xi_j(1 tensor m)) uniformly by a seminorm r on M. Joint continuity of multiplication in B then gives, for every output seminorm, a projective input seminorm controlling all the extended coefficient maps. The images of the bounded vectors y_j remain bounded in P_B(M). The summable coefficient sequence is unchanged. The resulting nuclear series agrees on the dense pure tensors with v_B, so v_B is B-nuclear. For Banach B this says in particular that all coefficient norms are bounded by one continuous seminorm on P_B(M). The same argument works when the target is a Hausdorff base-changed module F_B rather than free: extend the map m |-> 1 tensor_A u(1 tensor m) using its B action.

Now take the subnuclear witness p:M->E with M nuclear and up A-nuclear. The action epsilon:A hat_tensor M->M is onto, since epsilon(1 tensor m)=m; its continuous complex-linear section shows it is open. The composite g=p epsilon:P=A hat_tensor M->E is an open surjection, and u'=ug is A-nuclear by the composition property. Put f'=fg, also surjective. P is nuclear and fully A-transverse by the free formula and contracted bar complex in BT-0-BT-2. For every transverse base algebra A_t, balanced right exactness BT-1 makes g_t:P_t->E_t onto. The images of (f_t-u_t)g_t and f_t-u_t therefore coincide. Their cokernels are the same algebraic A_t-module.

We can arrange an A-nuclear representation u'(x)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(x)y_j in which y_j tends to zero. Starting with bounded y_j, choose integers N_k increasing to infinity so that sum_(j>=N_k)|lambda_j|<=2^(-2k). Put c_j=2^k for N_k<=j<N_(k+1), and c_j=1 on the initial block. Then c_j tends to infinity and sum_j c_j|lambda_j| is finite. Replace lambda_j by c_j lambda_j and y_j by y_j/c_j; this changes neither u' nor the equicontinuous coefficients, and makes y_j tend to zero in every target seminorm. Finite nonzero representations can be treated by appending zero terms.

Open surjectivity of f':P->F lets this null sequence be lifted to a null sequence x_j in P. Explicitly choose a decreasing neighbourhood basis V_n of zero in P that controls the first n defining seminorms by 2^(-n). Each f'(V_n) is a neighbourhood in F. Select increasing indices J_n such that y_j belongs to f'(V_n) whenever j>=J_n. For J_n<=j<J_(n+1), choose x_j in V_n with f'(x_j)=y_j; choose the finitely many initial lifts arbitrarily. These x_j tend to zero, hence form a bounded sequence. The series v(x)=sum_j lambda_j xi_j(x)x_j defines an A-nuclear endomorphism of P. Continuity of f' and convergence of the series give f'v=u'. Thus f'-u'=f'(I_P-v).

For any transverse A_t, f'_t remains surjective by BT-1. Hence it induces a surjection from P_t/(I_(P_t)-v_t)P_t onto F_t/(f'_t-u'_t)P_t. Together with the earlier equality of images, proving finite generation for I-v on the free module after shrinking proves it for the original f-u. The same free-witness argument and extension of its nuclear representation show that base-changing an A-subnuclear map between transverse nuclear modules yields a subnuclear map over the new nuclear algebra. Its source witness is the Hausdorff free module B hat_tensor M, even when B hat_tensor_A M itself has not been proved Hausdorff.

proofs.title: Subnuclear perturbation after shrinking a fully nuclear algebra
proofs.statement: Let A be fully nuclear, E,F fully A-transverse nuclear Frechet A-modules, f:E->F surjective and u:E->F A-subnuclear. For every 0<t<1, F_t/(f_t-u_t)E_t is finitely generated as an algebraic A_t-module. Neither closedness of (f_t-u_t)E_t nor Hausdorffness of this cokernel is claimed.
proof: Use RP-4 to reduce to P=A hat_tensor M and an A-nuclear endomorphism v of P, where it suffices to prove that the cokernel of I_(P_t)-v_t is a finitely generated A_t-module. Fix t<1 and let B_t be the Banach completion of A for p_t. The canonical A->B_t followed by B_t->A_t equals A->A_t: the latter map from B_t exists because p_r<=p_t for r<t, as established in RP-1.

Extend v to the free Frechet B_t-module S=B_t hat_tensor M using RP-4. The extension v_B is B_t-nuclear. RP-3 gives an integer N and continuous B_t-linear maps R_B:S->S, gamma_B:S->B_t^N and Y_B:B_t^N->S satisfying I_S=(I_S-v_B)R_B+Y_B gamma_B. These are maps between free modules over B_t, including its finite free module B_t^N.

Extend those maps along B_t->A_t by RP-4. Their domains and codomains become P_t=A_t hat_tensor M and A_t^N. Functoriality preserves both composition and addition, and (v_B)_(A_t)=v_t. Therefore I_(P_t)=(I_(P_t)-v_t)R_t+Y_t gamma_t. For every z in P_t this identity writes its cokernel class as the A_t-linear combination, with coefficients gamma_t(z), of the N classes of Y_t(e_1),...,Y_t(e_N). It is an actual equality before taking the quotient, not a statement about density of a finitely generated image in a completion.

The surjection of cokernels from RP-4 now gives finite generation for F_t/(f_t-u_t)E_t. No step forms a completed tensor of the possibly non-Hausdorff Banach-stage cokernel. The assertion is therefore at exactly its algebraic strength. It supplies the perturbation input for the next finite-complex argument, but does not itself identify cohomology sheaves, give a point-fibre comparison or prove the retained S6 theorem.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Use the nuclear algebra, balanced tensor, transverse module and radius conventions of RP and BT. Algebraic cohomology can be non-Hausdorff; no closure of a boundary space is inserted.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Complexes are cochain complexes. Bounded above means zero in degrees greater than one fixed integer. A finite-free-term complex may extend indefinitely towards negative degrees. It is called bounded only after both ends have been bounded.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: For h:L->E the comparison complex is C(h)^k=L^k direct_sum E^(k-1), with D(l,e)=(d_L l,h(l)-d_E e). This is the verified BT-5 convention. Every shift and every new generator below uses this same differential.

conventions.label: Convention
conventions.text: Complex analytic spaces are Hausdorff and retain their full local quotient structure. Closed embeddings and coherent modules are understood scheme-theoretically, not after reduction.

proofs.title: Finite generation of the highest remaining cohomology after shrinking
proofs.statement: Let A be fully nuclear and f:E->F a quasi-isomorphism of bounded-above complexes of fully transverse nuclear A-modules. Assume every f^k is A-subnuclear. If E and F have zero cohomology above q, then H^q(E_t) and H^q(F_t) are finitely generated A_t-modules for every t<1. The same statement applies after any initial radius restriction, with radii rescaled as in RP-1.
proof: For k>=q, acyclicity in degree k+1 gives strict exact sequences 0->Z^k(E)->E^k->Z^(k+1)(E)->0. The cycle spaces are closed nuclear modules. Starting above a common upper bound and descending, BT-4 makes each Z^k(E), k>=q, fully A-transverse; the same holds for F. These exact sequences also identify the base change of Z^k with the cycle space after restriction. In particular F^q/Z^q(F) is topologically Z^(q+1)(F), and is fully transverse. Surjectivity onto this closed cycle space gives the quotient topology by open mapping.

Choose an intermediate radius s with t<s<1. Restricting f^q on its source to Z^q(E) preserves subnuclearity by BT-6. Its image lies in Z^q(F), but subnuclearity into that closed target is not inferred directly. Apply RP-0 to the scalar-nuclear map A->A_s. Its transverse hypotheses hold for Z^q(E), F^q and F^q/Z^q(F) by the preceding paragraph. Thus g:Z^q(E_s)->Z^q(F_s) is A_s-subnuclear.

BT-5 makes f_s a quasi-isomorphism. Hence a:F_s^(q-1) direct_sum Z^q(E_s)->Z^q(F_s), a(y,z)=d_F y+g(z), is surjective: the class of any target cycle has a preimage under H^q(f_s), and the remaining difference is a boundary. All three modules here are fully A_s-transverse, and a is a continuous open surjection of Frechet spaces. The map u(y,z)=g(z) is A_s-subnuclear by composition. RP-5 applied to a-u gives a finitely generated cokernel after passing from A_s to A_t; this is a permissible radius t/s in A_s by RP-1.

The changed map a-u is d_F on the first summand and zero on the second. The cycle identifications from the first paragraph show that its cokernel is exactly Z^q(F_t)/d_F(F_t^(q-1))=H^q(F_t), not its Hausdorff completion. BT-5 identifies that module with H^q(E_t). This proves the assertion at its algebraic strength and does not require a closed coboundary space.

proofs.title: Comparison of cones and attachment of one finite free term
proofs.statement: A quasi-isomorphism f:E->F induces a quasi-isomorphism C(h)->C(fh), (l,e)|->(l,f(e)). For a finite-free partial complex L in degrees >=q, generators of H^q(C(h)) represented by cycles specify an additional term L^(q-1), with the exact signs needed to kill that cohomology group while leaving all higher groups unchanged.
proof: The displayed cone map is a chain map: applying its differential on either side gives (d_L l,f h(l)-f d_E e), since f d_E=d_F f. Its action on cohomology can be checked without a topological five-lemma assumption. For injectivity, suppose a closed (l,e) maps to D(a,b) in C(fh). Then l=d_L a and f(e-h(a))=-d_F b. Also d_E(e-h(a))=0 by the cycle and chain-map equations. Injectivity of H^(k-1)(f) implies e-h(a)=d_E c for some c. Thus (l,e)=D(a,-c) in C(h), proving injectivity.

For surjectivity, take a cycle (l,z) of degree k in C(fh). Its equations are d_L l=0 and d_F z=f h(l). Injectivity of H^k(f) shows h(l)=d_E e for some e of degree k-1. Then (l,e) is a cycle of C(h). The difference z-f(e) is a cycle in F^(k-1). Surjectivity of H^(k-1)(f) supplies a closed c in E^(k-1) and b in F^(k-2) with z-f(e)-f(c)=d_F b. Hence (l,z) and the image of (l,e+c) differ by D(0,-b), so they define the same cohomology class.

Now let L be zero below q, and suppose C(h) is acyclic in degrees greater than q. Choose finitely many cycles w_j=(a_j,b_j) in C(h)^q=L^q direct_sum E^(q-1) whose classes generate H^q(C(h)). Set L^(q-1)=A^r, d_L^(q-1)(e_j)=a_j and h^(q-1)(e_j)=b_j. The cycle equations say d_L^q a_j=0 and h^q(a_j)=d_E^(q-1)b_j. Therefore the enlarged L is a complex and the enlarged h is a chain map. Maps from finite free modules are continuous because they are finite sums of multiplication by the specified vectors.

In the new comparison complex the only new summand is L^(q-1) in degree q-1. Its differential to degree q sends (v,e) to (d_L^(q-1)v,h^(q-1)v-d_E e). Thus the new degree-q boundary space is the old boundary space plus the A-span of w_j. Those classes generate all degree-q cohomology, so that group becomes zero. Degree-q cycles and all groups in larger degrees are unchanged. This proves the inductive attachment with the actual differential, not an unspecified identification up to sign.

proofs.title: Construction over one common final radius
proofs.statement: Under the hypotheses on E,F,f in FC-0, without its upper cohomological vanishing hypothesis, for every 0<t<1 there is a bounded-above complex L of finite free A_t-modules and a quasi-isomorphism h:L->E_t. No lower bound is asserted here.
proof: Let N bound the degrees of E and F above. Set r_(N+1)=1 and r_q=t+(1-t)2^(q-N-1) for all integers q<=N. Then t<r_q<r_(q+1)<=1 and the decreasing radii tend to t as q tends to minus infinity. Each individual r_q is strictly greater than the final t. Start at q=N+1 with the zero partial complex L and its zero map into E over A. Its cone is E[-1] and vanishes above N+1. This gives the induction invariant with no unproved initial finite-generation assertion.

Assume the finite partial complex in degrees >=q has been constructed over A_(r_q), together with h into E_(r_q), and its cone M is acyclic above q. Let Ncone=C(f_(r_q) h). FC-1 gives a quasi-isomorphism M->Ncone. Both complexes are bounded above and their terms are fully transverse nuclear modules: each term is a direct sum of a finite free module and a term of E or F. The comparison in degree k is Id_(L^k) direct_sum f_(r_q)^(k-1). Identity on a finite free module is nuclear over the base algebra using its coordinate functionals and finitely many basis vectors. RP-4 preserves subnuclearity of f under radius restriction; BT-6 handles the two summands. Therefore this cone comparison satisfies FC-0.

Apply FC-0 from radius r_q to r_(q-1). It supplies finitely many generators for H^q(M_(r_(q-1))). Choose cycle representatives and use FC-1 to attach L^(q-1) and its maps. BT-4 preserves the previous acyclicity above q during this base change; the attachment kills degree q as well. The induction invariant therefore holds with q replaced by q-1. All previously chosen terms and maps are retained by restriction, not replaced by incompatible new choices.

For each fixed degree k, restrict the finite free module L^k and its maps from their construction radius to A_t. This defines one complex over A_t with each rank finite. Its differentials square to zero and h is a chain map because each identity already held at a finite stage. There is no inverse limit of complexes or infinite intersection of arbitrary neighbourhoods in this definition; every term is specified at one radius containing the fixed final domain.

To prove h is a quasi-isomorphism in degree k, choose an induction stage q<=k-1. Its cone is acyclic in degree k and above q. BT-4 preserves this upper acyclicity on restriction to A_t. The final cone and that restricted partial cone have identical terms and differentials in degrees k-1,k,k+1, since later attachments occur below those degrees. Their degree-k cohomology is therefore identical and zero. As this applies to every integer k, C(h) is acyclic. The exact cone criterion BT-5 proves h is a quasi-isomorphism. The construction may continue indefinitely to the left; boundedness below will be obtained separately on the curve.

proofs.title: Finite acyclic-cover comparison with explicit signs
proofs.statement: For a finite open cover U_1,...,U_m and a sheaf G whose positive cohomology vanishes on every nonempty finite intersection, the alternating Cech complex computes H^*(union U_i,G). Its comparison is natural under restrictions and refinements preserving the index order. The same construction gives a comparison of complexes of sheaves after direct image.
proof: The alternating differential is (delta c)_(i_0,...,i_(p+1))=sum_(a=0)^(p+1)(-1)^a c_(i_0,...,omit i_a,...,i_(p+1)) restricted to the intersection. Each double omission occurs twice with opposite signs, so delta squared is zero. Degree p uses only increasing index tuples and is zero for p>=m. Empty intersections contribute the zero group.

First consider a flabby sheaf J. Its augmented alternating complex is exact for every finite cover. Prove this by induction on m. Degree-zero exactness is the sheaf gluing axiom. For a positive-degree cocycle, write a for components not involving the last index, and b for components involving it. If the degree is p, the second part has degree p-1 on the cover (U_i intersection U_m)_(i<m), and the differential on the two parts is (delta a,delta b+(-1)^(p+1)res(a)). Induction makes a=delta u; subtract the coboundary of the cochain u with zero last-index components. The remaining second part b' is a cocycle. For p>=2 it is a boundary by induction on the intersection cover. For p=1 it glues to a section on (union_(i<m) U_i) intersection U_m. Flabbiness extends this section to U_m; its degree-zero cochain supported on U_m has precisely b' as its coboundary. Thus every positive cocycle is a boundary.

Choose an injective resolution J^bullet of G as a sheaf of modules. Its restrictions to open sets are injective, since extension by zero for an open immersion is an exact left adjoint to restriction. Injective sheaves of modules are flabby: the inclusion of the extension by zero of the structure sheaf of an open subset into the structure sheaf of the whole space, followed by injectivity of J, shows that every section on the open subset extends. These facts also apply after restriction. Thus Gamma(U_I,J^bullet) computes H^*(U_I,G), and each augmented horizontal Cech row for J^q is exact by the previous paragraph.

We also record why flabby resolutions, used below after closed pushforward, are acyclic resolutions. In a short exact sequence 0->J->M->N->0 with J flabby, every section s of N on an open W lifts to M(W). Choose local lifts on a covering and well-order its members. Given a lift on the union of earlier members, its difference from the next local lift is a J-section on the overlap. Extend that section to the new member by flabbiness and correct the new lift before gluing. At limit stages the previously compatible sections glue. This constructs a lift on all W. If M is also flabby, N is flabby: lift a section on a smaller open to M there, extend it using M, and take its image. Embed a flabby J in an injective sheaf and repeat on the quotient; the injectives and all successive quotients are flabby by these facts. The resulting injective resolution remains exact after sections on every open. Thus positive cohomology of a flabby sheaf vanishes. More generally an acyclic resolution computes derived sections: in each fixed positive degree, its successive kernel short exact sequences and the long exact derived-functor sequence dimension-shift finitely many times to identify the resolution cohomology with that of its initial sheaf. The same reasoning on inverse images of opens proves the direct-image version.

Form C^(p,q)=product_(|I|=p+1) Gamma(U_I,J^q), with total differential delta+(-1)^p d_J. Restriction commutes with d_J, so the two mixed terms cancel and this differential squares to zero. The map Gamma(union U_i,J^bullet)->Tot(C) lands in column p=0. It is a quasi-isomorphism: in a total cocycle eliminate the highest nonzero positive-p component using horizontal exactness, subtracting a total coboundary at p-1. The new vertical contribution has smaller p. Repetition leaves p=0, where horizontal closedness identifies a global section; the total cycle equation then identifies a global cocycle. The identical elimination on a primitive proves injectivity on cohomology. There are finitely many columns, so the process terminates.

On the other hand, positive cohomology of each intersection vanishes by hypothesis. The map Cech(U,G)->Tot(C) is a quasi-isomorphism: starting with the lowest-p component of a total cocycle that has q>0, its vertical differential is zero, so vertical exactness supplies a primitive. Subtract its total differential, with the sign (-1)^p, to remove that component. The added horizontal contribution has larger p and smaller q. Repeating ends in q=0, where the vertical kernel is Gamma(U_I,G), giving a Cech cocycle. For injectivity apply the same elimination to a primitive whose differential is a q=0 Cech cochain; its positive-q components can again be removed, leaving a primitive in the Cech complex. Each fixed total degree has only finitely many bidegrees, so no convergence assertion about an infinite sum is used.

Both arrows in this zigzag come from augmentations and restrictions, not from the choices made during the proof of exactness. They commute with restriction of opens and with index-preserving refinement. They therefore identify a cover-refinement map with the identity on sheaf cohomology of the same space. Applied on inverse images of base opens, the zigzag consists of morphisms of sheaf complexes on the base as well. This supplies the finite comparison needed here without leaving the Leray step as an unexamined external tag.

proofs.title: Properness supplies two compatible finite graph covers
proofs.statement: Let f:X->B be a proper holomorphic map to a Riemann surface and G a coherent sheaf on the full analytic space X. Near any b in B there are finite alternating Cech complexes E,F of fully transverse nuclear O(D)-modules, bounded in nonnegative degrees, and a degreewise O(D)-subnuclear quasi-isomorphism E->F. Their terms restrict by balanced tensor to the actual section complexes over every Stein subopen of D.
proof: Choose coordinate discs D compactly contained in D_0, with closure(D_0) contained in a further coordinate disc D_1 about b. Restrict X to f^(-1)(D_1), preserving properness over D_1. The set K=f^(-1)(closure(D_0)) is compact. Around each point choose an analytic chart U_i^0 closed in a Stein open Omega_i^0 and smaller Stein polydiscs Omega_i' compactly contained in Omega_i compactly contained in Omega_i^0. A finite selection can be made so that the U_i'=U_i^0 intersection Omega_i' cover K. Put U_i=U_i^0 intersection Omega_i. Both indexed families then cover f^(-1)(D). This uses compactness of K, not compactness of X.

For an increasing tuple I, the diagonal chart map embeds U_I^0=intersection_(i in I) U_i^0 as a closed full analytic subspace of Omega_I^0=product_(i in I) Omega_i^0. This is precisely the full closed-intersection argument of the pinned finiteness provider, Lemma 1.1: a convergent tuple of images has a common limit because X is Hausdorff; locally the map is the graph of holomorphic coordinate representatives, with its original ideal and graph equations. Appending f gives a closed full graph embedding U_I^0->Omega_I^0 x D_1. Closedness follows also by continuity of f; locally its graph adds the equation for the base coordinate to the same full ideal. Let G_I be the coherent pushforward of G along that embedding.

Write Omega_I=product Omega_i and Omega_I'=product Omega_i'. Restricting the graph to Omega_I x D gives U_I intersection f^(-1)(D), and restricting to Omega_I' x D gives the corresponding primed intersection. In particular their G sections are respectively Gamma(Omega_I x D,G_I) and Gamma(Omega_I' x D,G_I). Product Stein manifolds and closed coherent pushforward, followed by Cartan B, show that all these intersections are acyclic for G. The same holds after replacing D by any Stein open V contained in D. Their local ideals and coefficient modules retain all nilpotents.

Use these sections as the factors of E^p=Cech^p(U intersection f^(-1)(D),G) and F^p for the primed cover. There are finitely many factors in each degree and no terms outside 0,...,m-1. NS-4 makes their section spaces nuclear; RP-2 makes them fully O(D)-transverse. More generally BT-3 applied to G_I on the ambient product identifies O(V) hat_tensor_(O(D)) each factor with Gamma(Omega_I x V,G_I), with positive Tor zero, for any Stein subopen V of D. Finite products preserve these statements. The identifications commute with all restriction maps in the Cech differential because they are induced by multiplication of holomorphic functions and section restriction.

Each Omega_I' is relatively compact in Omega_I and both lie relatively compactly in Omega_I^0. BT-6 therefore makes the restriction of the I-th factor O(D)-subnuclear. The finite product of these restrictions is subnuclear by finite sums and composition. These maps form a chain map E->F. By the acyclic-cover comparison FC-3 both complexes compute H^*(f^(-1)(D),G), and the restriction chain map induces the identity under that identification. It is consequently a quasi-isomorphism. This verifies the needed hypotheses on every intersection, not only on the individual chart sections.

proofs.title: The analytic relative complex and coherent direct images
proofs.statement: For the proper map and coherent sheaf of FC-4, after shrinking about any base point there is a bounded-above finite-free-term holomorphic sheaf complex L representing Rf_*G. Its comparison with the finite Cech complex is a quasi-isomorphism on every Stein subopen of that neighbourhood. In particular all R^q f_*G are coherent there. This statement does not require flatness.
proof: Apply FC-2 to the O(D)-complexes and restriction map constructed in FC-4. For a fixed t<1 it produces finite free O(D_t)-modules L^k, zero for k>m-1, and a chain map h:L->E_t that is a quasi-isomorphism. Each differential is a finite matrix of functions holomorphic on D_t, so it defines a differential between finite free sheaves on D_t. Matrix multiplication and h's equations show these are genuine complexes and sheaf morphisms. A map h^k from a finite free module is specified by finitely many sections of the k-th Cech term; their restrictions define h over every smaller open.

For every Stein V contained in D_t, finite free L^k are transverse to O(V) by BT-0-BT-2. FC-4 and BT-3 make the E_t terms transverse as well and identify their balanced tensors with the actual Cech section terms over f^(-1)(V). Thus BT-5 applied to h gives a quasi-isomorphism L(V)->Cech(U intersection f^(-1)(V),G). The maps commute with restriction of V because both the free matrices and all comparison vectors are restrictions of their fixed sections on D_t. No point-fibre assertion is inferred from this open-restriction statement.

For an explicit derived comparison, choose an injective resolution J of G on f^(-1)(D_t). The sheaf on D_t of k-th Cech sections assigns V the product of Gamma(U_I intersection f^(-1)(V),G). FC-3 supplies sheaf-complex maps from that Cech complex to Tot(Cech(U,J)) and from f_*J to the same total complex. On the Stein basis each is a quasi-isomorphism by the argument of FC-3 and the acyclicity of the intersections. Filtered colimits of modules are exact: a finite equation between germs holds on some common smaller neighbourhood, which proves both preservation of kernels in finite exact diagrams and lifting for cokernels. Passing to stalks therefore shows these maps, and h, are quasi-isomorphisms of sheaf complexes. This actual zigzag identifies L with Rf_*G, rather than merely giving abstract isomorphisms between its cohomology dimensions.

In every fixed degree, H^q(L)=ker(d^q)/image(d^(q-1)) is coherent by Oka coherence and the kernel, image and cokernel properties in the pinned coherent-sheaf provider. Only three finite free terms enter this assertion, so infinitely many possible negative terms cause no problem. The derived comparison gives H^q(L)=R^q f_*G. These sheaves vanish for negative q, since f_*J has no negative terms. This proves direct-image coherence on the base curve with full analytic source structure, conditional only on the explicitly bound analytic prerequisites already supplied.

proofs.title: Bounded truncation on the curve without making cohomology locally free
proofs.statement: The relative representative L of FC-5 can be replaced, near any chosen b, by a bounded complex P of finite free holomorphic sheaves. This supplies the boundedness required in the retained S6 obligation; it does not assert local freeness of any R^q f_*G.
proof: Let I=image(d_L^(-1):L^(-1)->L^0). It is coherent and is a subsheaf of finite free L^0. The local ring A=O_(B,b) is a discrete valuation ring: in a coordinate z vanishing at b, every nonzero convergent power series is z^n times a unit, and the unit has a convergent inverse on a smaller disc. For completeness, the image of any finite matrix over this ring is finite free. If the matrix is nonzero, move an entry of least valuation to its upper left corner. It divides every other entry. Invertible row and column operations clear its column and row. Repeat on the smaller remaining matrix. This gives a diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries and zero remainder, whose nonzero columns are a free basis for its image. The invertible operations transport that basis back. Apply this to d_L^(-1) on stalks to see I_b is finite free.

Represent a basis of I_b by finitely many local sections of I, obtaining a morphism O^r->I that is an isomorphism at b. Its kernel and cokernel are coherent. A finite-type sheaf with zero stalk at b vanishes in a neighbourhood: take finitely many local generators and shrink until each of their zero germs is zero as a section. Apply this to kernel and cokernel, shrinking once more. Thus I is a finite free sheaf there. This is a local property of the image submodule over a smooth curve, not a claim that its quotient or the cohomology sheaves are free.

Define P^q=0 for q<-1, P^(-1)=I, and P^q=L^q for q>=0, with its first differential the inclusion I->L^0 and all later differentials unchanged. It is a complex because d_L^0 kills I. Define L->P by d_L^(-1) with codomain I in degree -1, identity in nonnegative degrees, and zero below -1. The chain equations follow from d_L squared=0. The entering image in degree zero is unchanged, so the map induces isomorphisms in all nonnegative cohomological degrees. P has no negative cohomology because its first differential is injective; L has none by FC-5. Hence L->P is a quasi-isomorphism. The complex P is finite free and lies in degrees [-1,m-1]. Together with the earlier zigzag it represents Rf_*G.

proofs.title: Canonical full-fibre comparison and the retained surface theorem
proofs.statement: Let f:X->B be proper and flat with B a Riemann surface, all full fibres pure of dimension two, and E a holomorphic vector bundle. Then R^q f_*E=0 for q>2, and at every b the canonical map (R^2 f_*E)_b tensor_(O_(B,b)) k(b)->H^2(X_b,E|_(X_b)) is an isomorphism. The bounded representative P of FC-6 has the canonical derived-fibre identification P_b tensor^L k(b) equivalent to RΓ(X_b,E|_(X_b)). No smoothness or compactness of X, reducedness of X_b, constancy of h^2, or local freeness of R^2 f_*E is imposed.
proof: We identify the canonical comparison using the full fibre, including its nonreduced structure. Fix b, take a base coordinate z with zero set {b}, put V=f^(-1)(U), and let i:X_b->V and j:{b}->U be the closed inclusions. Flatness of f and local freeness of E give an exact sequence 0->E --f^*z--> E -> i_*E_b->0. The last term is E/(f^*z)E on the full fibre O_V/(f^*z), not the module on its reduction.

Choose an injective resolution J of E on V and set K=f_*J. Multiplication by f^*z acts on J. The usual cone has Cone(z:J->J)^q=J^q direct_sum J^(q+1), with differential (a,c)|->(d_J a+z c,-d_J c). Its cohomology is concentrated in degree zero and equals i_*E_b, by the exact sequence above. Its terms are finite sums of flabby sheaves, hence acyclic for f_*: over every base open their sections are those of flabby sheaves on its inverse image. It therefore computes Rf_*i_*E_b. Applying f_* commutes with these finite sums and the scalar action, giving Cone(z:K->K) on the nose.

Let T=[O_U --z--> O_U] in degrees -1,0, resolving j_*k(b). A bounded complex of flat modules preserves acyclic complexes under tensor: one flat module preserves kernels and images of each differential in an exact complex, and a finite complex follows by its successive finite-term filtration. Thus T is K-flat and K tensor T computes K tensor^L j_*k(b). In total degree q write its components as (a,c) in K^q direct_sum K^(q+1); the differential is (d_K a+(-1)^(q+1)z c,d_K c). The map (a,c)|->(a,(-1)^(q+1)c) identifies it with Cone(z:K->K) with the differential in the previous paragraph. This checks the derived tensor identification including its sign.

A flabby resolution on X_b stays flabby and exact after the closed pushforward i_*. Consequently Rf_*i_*E_b is j_*RΓ(X_b,E_b). Taking the stalk at b gives (Rf_*E)_b tensor_A^L k(b) equivalent to RΓ(X_b,E_b), where A=O_(B,b). Composing with the actual derived identification of P in FC-6 gives the asserted comparison for P. The map is induced by the restriction E->i_*E_b. In particular its map from ordinary cohomology modulo z is the canonical base-change map, not an isomorphism selected from a dimension count. If the coordinate changes to uz for a unit u, the chain map T_(uz)->T_z is multiplication by u in degree -1 and identity in degree zero; it commutes with the differentials and the augmentations. Thus the derived morphism is independent of that choice and of the chosen resolutions.

Set M^q=(R^q f_*E)_b. The cone exact sequence now yields 0->M^q/zM^q->H^q(X_b,E_b)->M^(q+1)[z]->0, where M[z] is the kernel of multiplication by z. The first arrow is the canonical map just identified. This exact sequence retains the torsion term; it is not set to zero in all degrees. Coherence from FC-5 makes every M^q a finite A-module. Properness makes X_b compact, and its full dimension is two. The pinned QG compact coherent dimension proof gives H^q(X_b,E_b)=0 for q>2, with the original nilpotent structure retained.

For q>2, the exact sequence implies M^q=zM^q. To see directly why this finite module is zero, take generators m_1,...,m_r and write m_i=z sum_j a_ij m_j. The matrix I-z(a_ij) annihilates the generator column. Multiplication by its adjugate shows det(I-z(a_ij)) annihilates every generator. Its residue is 1, so it is a unit of the local ring; therefore M^q=0. This works at every b and proves R^q f_*E=0 for q>2. In degree two the same exact sequence has M^3[z]=0 and supplies the canonical isomorphism claimed. None of these steps uses local freeness of M^2 or constancy of the fibre cohomology dimension.
